articleTitle: A Two-Terminal, Broadband, Low-Energy Optical Synaptic Device for Optical Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this work, we propose a two-terminal, broadband Pd/CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>/ITO optical synapse with an ultra-low energy consumption of 42.5 fJ per operation. With a read voltage as low as 0.04 V, the optical synapse demonstrates light-dosage-tunable and wavelength-dependent synaptic plasticity. The light dosage tunable plasticity enables in-sensor optical temporal information encoding. Consequently, the two-terminal oxide-based optical synapse offers itself as an efficient solution for future neuromorphic vision processing systems with broadband photoresponse and exceptionally low energy consumption.

articleTitle: Design and Study of Microfluidic Chip for Isolation of Circulating Tumor Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: More than 90% of cancer-related deaths are caused by cancer cell metastasis. During the tumor metastasis process, tumor cells are shed from the primary tumor tissue into the blood, become circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and further spread to distant organs. In order to isolate circulating tumor cells from blood containing a variety of cells, this paper introduces a new high-efficiency microfluidic chip based on micropillar arrays to isolate CTCs from the blood of cancer patients, providing prognostic information and monitoring for cancer patients. treatment effect. By simulating the capture rate and separation efficiency of rhombus micropillar chips and rectangular micropillar chips, a rhombus micropillar separation chip was designed and manufactured. Through COMSOL, we conducted numerical simulations to compare the velocity and pressure distribution inside the micropillar array, and simulated the chip capture rate. Diamond shaped microcolumns have a higher capture rate 85%, while rectangular microcolumns only have 73%. The diamond-shaped column separation chip provides a novel micro-column structure for the separation, detection and staining of CTCs on the chip. In the future, this possibility could be extended to the culture of captured CTCs.

articleTitle: Bonding Process for Micro-LEDs on Polyimide Sacrificial Layer Supporting Laser-Induced Mass Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study introduces a novel bonding technique utilizing a polyimide (PI) sacrificial layer for the laser-induced mass transfer of micro-light-emitting diodes (Micro-LEDs). We propose a set of bonding process parameters and investigate the impact of applying pressure during the bonding procedure. The efficiency of the bonding process is quantitatively assessed by defining the bonding success ratio and the embedding depth ratio. To investigate the removal of excess sacrificial layers and sidewall residues, oxygen reactive ion etching (RIE) is employed on the bonded Micro-LEDs. The effectiveness of RIE is demonstrated by measuring the embedding depth ratio with a white light interferometer and conducting morphological analysis of the Micro-LEDs using a scanning electron microscope. Furthermore, to verify the complete removal of almost all excess PI sacrificial layers, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy is employed on the sacrificial layer before and after RIE treatment.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Sub-Arc-Second Micro-Drive Rotary Mechanism Based on Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The structural design optimization of the micro-rotating mechanism is to achieve the maximum rotation output angle under the same input conditions within a certain range of spatial motion, so as to achieve the purpose of improving the motion compensation range of the micro-rotating mechanism. In view of the shortcomings of small motion travel space, low positioning accuracy and small sub-arc second, a miniature rotary drive mechanism was designed, and its structure was optimized to achieve the aim of large output angle. The first is to design a micro-drive rotating mechanism that can accurately convert the linear motion input as piezoelectric ceramics into the output as rotary motion. Secondly, the particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to optimize the structure of the micro-rotating mechanism. Then, the kinematic performance of the optimized micro-rotating mechanism was analyzed by the finite element method. From the results, it can be seen that the optimized micro-motion rotation mechanism meets the purpose of the design use. The motion range of the optimized micro-rotating mechanism is 57.5% higher than that of the preoptimized micro-rotating mechanism, and its finite element analysis error is 8.27%. Its motion accuracy reaches sub-arc-seconds. This study is a reference for the study of ultra-precise positioning.

articleTitle: Study on Cavitation Behavior of Fan Impeller under Different Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study investigates the cavitation behavior of fan impellers under different working conditions using Fluent simulation analysis. The working fluids considered include cryogenic liquid oxygen, cryogenic liquid nitrogen, and air, selected for their distinct physical properties and industrial relevance. The impeller's rotational speed and fluid inlet flow rate significantly impact cavitation performance. Simulation results indicate that cryogenic fluids exhibit higher cavitation risks, particularly at the inlet, due to rapid vaporization caused by low pressures. Higher rotational speeds and fluid inlet flow rates exacerbate cavitation by increasing pressure fluctuations and reducing local static pressures below the vapor pressure, leading to bubble formation and collapse. This research highlights the critical need for optimizing impeller design and operating conditions to mitigate cavitation damage and enhance the efficiency and lifespan of fan systems.

articleTitle: Thermal Denaturation of IgE Molecules Visualized by Atomic Force Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, the process of thermal denaturation of Immunoglobulin E (IgE) molecules was visualized and characterized by atomic force microscopy (AFM). It was found that high temperature and heating conditions make IgE molecules lose their natural structure, causing them to aggregate and form flower-like morphologies with high middle and low sides. In addition, the height and area of IgE aggregates were proportional to both temperature and heating time. These results not only provide a basis for us to understand the thermal denaturation process of IgE, but also provide valuable reference information for studying the influence of external factors on protein molecules.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Fractional Order PID Control of Micro Nano Positioning Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Micro-nano positioning technology is utilized in various fields, including biomedical engineering, micro-assembly, cell injection, and microchip manufacturing, and so on. Among these technologies, the piezoelectric-driven micro-nano positioning platform, which employs a piezoelectric ceramic actuator as the driving device, is one of the most commonly used positioning devices in micro positioning applications. However, the hysteresis of piezoelectric ceramic (PZT) actuators adversely affects the positioning accuracy of these platforms. In this paper, we propose a fuzzy fractional-order PID (FFOPID) controller to compensate for the hysteresis behavior of piezoelectric ceramics. This controller integrates fuzzy theory, where the membership functions and fuzzy rules are designed to create a FFOPID controller capable of mitigating the hysteresis effects of piezoelectric ceramics. Experimental results demonstrate that the FFOPID controller effectively reduces the rate-dependent hysteresis of the micro-nano positioning platform, thereby enhancing the adaptability and precision of the control system.

Author Keywords: control system of micro-nano positioning stage

articleTitle: Controlling the Solid-State Nanopore Size Using Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: At present, nanopores have received widespread attention because of their single-molecule scale detection accuracy. Solid-state nanopores have the advantages of stability, tolerance, easy integration and controllability. The size and shape of the nanopore will directly affect the detection accuracy of the solid-state nanopore sensor. Therefore, the controllable preparation of the solid-state nanopore plays a crucial role. This paper reports a simple method for changing pore diameter via applying a voltage bias across the pore. The amplitude of voltage bias determines shrinkage or enlargement of the nanopore. The nanopores we fabricated have successfully been used to detect DNA and protein molecules and show a good noise level.

articleTitle: Study of a Dynamic Impedance Matching Method for Ultrasonic Bone Knife Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Since the stability of the working performance of ultrasonic bone knife transducer is closely related to the dynamic impedance matching, this paper designs a dynamic impedance matching closed-loop control system. The dynamic impedance calculation model of ultrasonic bone knife transducer is established, and on this basis, the voltage, current true RMS value and dynamic impedance phase monitoring circuit and variable inductance adjustment circuit are designed during the working process of ultrasonic bone knife transducer, and the real-time calculation of impedance matching inductance is realized. The impedance matching closed-loop control system was also tested, and the experimental results show that the dynamic impedance matching method can satisfy the ultrasonic bone knife transducer working in a purely resistive state, and the steady state output amplitude of the current is significantly improved compared with that before the matching, which further lays down a foundation for the frequency tracking control of the ultrasonic bone knife transducer.

articleTitle: Study of the Functional Properties of Single Nanowires of ZnO for Photonic and Biochemical Nanosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Individual nanorods of ZnO are promising objects for optical and chemical sensing. We fabricate prototypes of UV and bionanosensors using a 3D nano-manipulation system from the nanorods synthesised by chemical vapour deposition (CVD). For the first time, we characterize the spectral response of individual ZnO nanorod to the UV-vis light, and we show its selective sensitivity to the UV range. We show that the liquid-gated device based on ZnO nanorod can be used as a bio-sensor, for example, for detecting hypoxanthine in pork meat.

articleTitle: Research on Photometric Traceability Technology of Multi-Parameter Rapid Food Tester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the increasing prominence of food safety issues, the application of multi-parameter rapid food testers is becoming more and more widespread. The aim of this paper was to address the need for metrological traceability of spectrophotometric multi-parameter rapid food testers for rapid food safety testing applications. In this paper, the photometric linear calibration device for multi-parameter food on-site rapid detector, a standard filter with a transmission ratio measurement range of 5% ∼ 90% and U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rel</inf>=0.4% ∼ 2.6% (k=2), was developed to address the need for photometric linear calibration of multi-parameter food on-site rapid detector in different nanometer bands. The developed absorbance linear solution standards included: potassium dichromate linear solution standards (0.1 μg/μL, 0.2 μg/μL, 0.4 μg/μL, 0.6 μg/μL), cobalt chloride linear solution standards (10 μg/μL, 20 μg/μL, 30 μg/μL, 40 μg/μL) and copper sulfate linear solution standards (10 μg/μL, 20 μg/μL, 40 μg/μL, 60 μg/μL), which could satisfy the requirements for linear calibration of the spectrophotometric calibration system in the range of 400 nm ∼ 600 nm. The developed fiber optic spectrometer for calibration of multi-parameter on-site rapid food tester proved to be effective in testing the wavelength accuracy of multi-parameter on-site rapid food tester, with the wavelength accuracy of the fiber optic spectrometer reaching ±1.0 nm. This study could effectively solve the demand for photometeric traceability of multi-parameter food rapid detectors, providing new scientific support for the rapid development and technological progress of rapid detection instruments.

articleTitle: Study on the Detection Method of Lipoprotein Phospholipase A2 Based on Nanomicrospheres
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: This study is based on the detection of Lp-PLA2 in serum using latex enhanced immunoturbidimetry (PETIA). Reform the existing process by selecting smaller particle size microspheres to increase the upper limit of linearity, selecting microspheres with fewer surface -COOH to ensure low sensitivity, and providing a more accurate and sensitive reagent kit for clinical use. Method: Determine the optimal reaction conditions, including Lp-PLA2 antibody manufacturer, nanoparticle size, antibody concentration, concentration of crosslinking agent [1- (3-dimethylaminopropyl) -3-ethylcarbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC)], pH value of coupling solution, and concentration of blocking agent. Establish a PETIA method for detecting serum Lp-PLA2. And evaluate its precision, linear range, and recovery rate for performance. Result: The Lp-PLA2 antibody and nanospheres from Huamei Biotechnology were selected as JSR-P0117, with the maximum absorbance range and the best linear relationship at an antibody concentration of 0.2 mg/mL; The optimal reaction conditions for PETIA include a crosslinking agent (EDC) concentration of 95 μg/mL, a blocking agent (10% BSA solution) concentration of 7 μL/mL, and a coupling buffer of boric acid buffer The optimal coupling rate is achieved at a pH value of 8.0. The established PETIA detection sample recovery rate is between 96% - 106%; Within batch coefficient of variation (CV) and between batches CV<2%; The linear range is 10-2100 ng/mL. Conclusion: Comparing to other methods, the PETIA established in this study for detecting Lp-PLA2 in serum is accurate, with a wide linear range, significantly better than the linear range of similar products on the market (20-1000 ng/mL). The experimental results provide laboratory guidance and reference for the development of Lp-PLA2 diagnostic kits.

articleTitle: Friction Characterization of Suspended Two-Dimensional Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The examination of two-dimensional materials is deemed imperative owing to their distinctive characteristics and potential applications spanning diverse domains. A comprehension of their atomic-level behavior empowers researchers to fully exploit their capabilities, thereby facilitating the advancement of innovative technologies and materials endowed with superior performance and functionality. Discrepancies in friction across samples characterized by varying contact stiffness prompt an investigation, which employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulation modeling of one-dimensional atomic chains constrained at both ends, alongside atomic force microscopy (AFM) experiments involving thin layers of graphite deposited onto grooved substrates. An observed trend reveals synchronized alterations in contact stiffness and friction, indicating an interrelation between the two phenomena. These collective findings contribute to a deeper elucidation of the intricate mechanisms governing friction at the nanoscale, with potential ramifications for the optimization of tribological performance across a spectrum of technological applications.

articleTitle: Design of a New Compliant Piezoelectric Microgripper with Parasitic Motion Self-Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a novel piezoelectric-driven symmetrical microgripper with parasitic motion self-compensation. For the first time, the microgripper achieve parasitic motion self-compensation for the gripping ends of the four-bar parallelogram mechanisms without using an extra actuator, which facilitates high precision gripping/releasing tasks. Its uniqueness is that the self-compensatory mechanism is integrated with the output end of the piezoelectric actuator to synchronously move the non-gripping ends of the four-bar parallelogram mechanisms to compensate for its parasitic motion in real time. The relationships between the structural parameters are studied by establishing analytical models. To obtain an anastomotic compensation of the self-compensatory mechanism and an expected performance of microgripper, the structural parameters are optimally tuned based on finite-element analysis simulation. With the optimal structural parameters, simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the parasitic motion compensation of the self-compensatory mechanisms.

articleTitle: Design and Assessment of 3-DOF Nano-Gimbal for Spatial Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: High-precision spatial manipulation and measurement require high-ratio vibration reduction and high positioning accuracy devices, in the presence of multi-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) vibrations and varying direction payload. In this paper, to ensure the positioning accuracy of the end-effector, a 3-DOF nano-gimbal is designed, which integrates a proposed 3-DOF tuned mass damper (TMD) for vibration suppression and a flexure-based nanopositioner for steady-state precision. Furthermore, as the critical part of vibration suppression, the modeling and design of 3-DOF TMD are analyzed and discussed in detail, considering both passive and active cases. First, the design and modeling of a 3-DOF nano-gimbal are presented, which is modeled by the modal decomposition method to obtain a set of decoupled motion equations. Then, the TMD is parameterized and optimized, where the passive case is designed by harmonic response methods, and the control law of the active case is designed by equivalent dynamics coefficients with state estimation. Finally, the performances of TMD and active tuned mass damper (ATMD) are evaluated by a set of simulations, including frequency and time domain assessments.

articleTitle: Microarray Fluorescence Image Processing and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Microarray chip technology has met the challenges of traditional fluorescent labeling in terms of high cost and low detection efficiency , and provides a high-throughput and cost-effective alternative detection scheme for the field of life science. This paper mainly focuses on the image preprocessing, image correction, image segmentation, speckle denoising and gray value experiment of microarray chip technology. Gaussian filter algorithm is used to reduce image noise quickly, histogram equalization method is used to enhance image contrast, Hoff transform method is established to realize fast and accurate image correction, and FCM image segmentation principle is derived to optimize the analysis state of part or whole image. The key points which affect the gray value are found out through the simulation experiment. This set of efficient image processing process significantly improves the speed and accuracy of microarray image analysis , and lays a solid technical foundation for the application and development of high-throughput biodetection technology.

articleTitle: Creation of the Nano-Soldering Technology for 3D Mechanical Bottomup Nano-Assembling of Individual Nanodevices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The paper reports the creation of a nano-soldering method in a circuit with tungsten microneedles separated by an air gap. An external voltage was applied to the microneedles separated by air gap. During the experiments, a plasma discharge, and the formation of metallic-organic composite "nano-fluff" on tungsten microneedles was observed. At the same time, the current-voltage characteristic (CVC) was studied. The CVC revealed the regions of negative differential resistance that arose at the moment of formation of the plasma discharge. In the three-needle design, the reliable electrical and mechanical contact was achieved between two microneedle due to nano-fluff formation, featuring a new approach to the creation of the nano-soldering technology for 3D mechanical bottom-up nano-assembling of individual nano-devices.

articleTitle: Establishment of a Detection Methodology for CAR-T Cell Vector Copy Number Using Droplet Digital PCR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: To explore the establishment of a detection method for the vectors copy number of Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells (CAR-T) in patients undergoing CAR-T immunotherapy, based on droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) technology, and to evaluate the performance of this method. Methods: Primers and probes were designed for the costimulatory CD28 gene of CAR-T drugs and the single-copy internal reference gene ALB, and a ddPCR reaction system was established. The accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, and precision of this method were assessed. Results: The ddPCR method demonstrated good accuracy and specificity in detecting standard samples. The method achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.05% for detecting the CD28 gene at a concentration of 400copies/pL, and the coefficient of variation (CV) values for both high and low precision standard samples were less than 5%. Conclusion: The ddPCR method can successfully detect the vectors copy number of CAR-T in patients undergoing CAR-T immunotherapy. It has the advantages of being simple, fast, highly sensitive, and highly specific, and it can truly achieve absolute quantification.

articleTitle: Positive Motion Control of a Piezo-Driven Flexure Micro-Positioning Stage for Chip Peeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The process of ejecting and peeling the chip from the blue tape can easily lead to chip damage. It is of great importance to realize positively synchronous control of motion and force exerted on the chip during the ejection process. This paper developed a piezo-driven flexure micro-positioning stage for chip ejection which can realize positively synchronous control of motion and force. A bridge-type flexure mechanism is designed and a PID closed-loop control is developed. Based on this system, the difference in the required driving voltage for the piezoelectric actuator with and without a load is analyzed and a force prediction model is developed. The system achieves self-prediction of the force reacted from the chip during the ejection process. Finally, positive control of the motion and force synchronously during the chip ejecting process is realized.

articleTitle: Effect of Functional Grading on the Performance of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Scaffolds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Porous scaffolds based on triply periodic minimal surface are a promising research direction in the field of bone scaffold design. Because of its excellent mechanical properties and easy programming, the triply periodic minimal surface scaffold can achieve more flexible functional grading, so it can be well used in the treatment of bone defects. In order to make the design of the bone scaffold better close to the natural bone tissue, it is necessary to design the functional grading of the scaffold. This paper is devoted to exploring the influence of the introduction of functional grading on the strength of scaffold. The scaffolds involved in this study are all based on the Gyroid surface in the triply periodic minimal surface. Two functional grading methods, porosity gradient scaffolds and pore size gradient scaffolds, are used in this work. It is found that stress concentration is common between transition layers of pore size gradient scaffolds. This conclusion provides an effective design basis and reference for the design of porous bone scaffolds and other porous structures.

articleTitle: Research on Image Sharpness Evaluation in Microstructure Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To address issues of insufficient sensitivity and weak anti-noise characteristics in existing image sharpness evaluation algorithms, we propose a method combining local variance and gradient analysis. Traditional methods like the Tenengrad function use horizontal and vertical gradient values, while multi-directional gradients can increase noise sensitivity and false detections. Our approach integrates the Tenengrad function with gray variance processing, analyzing the deviation of each pixel's brightness from the average to distinguish content from background. Normalizing these values helps reduce background and impurity pixel influence. Preprocessing with an anisotropic diffusion filter smooths the image while preserving edges. Experimental results show this method offers higher sensitivity and better noise resistance than traditional functions, suitable for autofocus systems.

articleTitle: Functional Properties of Cold-Rolled Rapidly Quenched Ribbons of Shape Memory TiNiCu Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Rapidly quenched thin TiNiCu alloy ribbons are precursors in the fabrication of micro- and nanotweezers for the manipulation of micro- and nanoscale objects. The thickness of the ribbons has been reduced by cold rolling in amorphous state. A thickness reduction rate of 1.2-1.5 times has been achieved by rolling with a load of up to 12 tons. We show that shape memory effect has been generated after isothermal crystallization in the rolled ribbons. The characteristic martensitic transformation temperatures have increased, the transformation hysteresis width has decreased and the shape memory effect has decreased slightly. The lateral roughness of the ribbon surfaces has decreased both for the contact and the reverse ribbon surfaces.

articleTitle: A Novel Fluorescence Assay for the Rapid Detection of 2019-nCoV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: To establish an immunological method for the detection of COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) based on the combination of a novel nanospheres fluorescent marker and immunochromatographyMethods: Quantum dot microspheres were prepared by membrane emulsification technology. The monoclonal antibody labeled with COVID-19 antigen and fluorescent microspheres were coupled to fluorescent markers through EDC and NHS. The quantitative test strip was established by combining immunochromatography with luminescence technology. Result: Quantum dot microsphere immunochromatographic test strips and colloidal gold immunochromatographic test strips simultaneously detected N protein recombinant antigen, Delta inactivated virus solution, and Gamma inactivated virus solution. The former had sensitivity 10 times higher than the latter in detecting N protein recombinant antigen Delta inactivated virus solution and Gamma inactivated virus solution, with a detection 3 times higher and a detection 100 times higher. Conclusion: The establishment of this detection method can more sensitively detect the coronavirus. After optimizing the detection method of this study, it can be used to supplement the existing detection technology gaps and provide faster, more sensitive, and convenient detection methods. At the same time, it provides experimental technology and application development support for the development of subsequent in vitro diagnostic products.

articleTitle: Friction Between a Hard Cylinder and a Soft Elastomer in Adhesive Contact: An Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The friction between a steel cylinder and a soft elastomer in adhesive contact is experimentally investigated as the normal force is gradually increased. The dependencies of normal and tangential forces, contact area, as well as average pressure and tangential stresses on the indentation depth, are analyzed. It is shown that the coefficient of friction decreases with increasing normal force according to a power law.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Sound Field Radiation Simulation for Nanochip Megasonic Cleaning Transducers Based on Comsol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the rapid development of the semiconductor industry, cleaning is widely used in fields such as chip manufacturing. Cleaning, as an important component of chip manufacturing processes, plays a crucial role in achieving nanoscale precision in chips. However, in the process of chip manufacturing, various pollutants and small particles are often adhered to the surface of the chip, which directly affect the quality and stability of the chip manufacturing process. Therefore, cleaning the chip has become particularly important. In the cleaning of nanochips, megasonic technology has demonstrated its unique advantages. Megasonic cleaning can remove small particles smaller than 0.2 g m and avoid potential damage to the surface of objects caused by cavitation. However, the distribution of water acoustic fields varies greatly among different matching layers. In order to further improve the cleaning efficiency of the nanochip megaacoustic cleaning transducer, increase the sound pressure in the water, and reduce the loss during energy transfer, this paper uses the finite element software Comsol to analyze the water acoustic field of the nanochip megaacoustic transducer. The influence of matching layer material and transducer oscillator structure size on the water acoustic pressure of the nanochip megaacoustic cleaning transducer is studied, and based on the analysis results, the optimized design of the nanochip megaacoustic transducer is carried out. The optimization results show that the spray type megaacoustic transducer with quartz as the matching layer has a greater water pressure amplitude than the water pressure amplitude with steel and aluminum as the matching layer, and still has a strong sound field intensity at a longer propagation distance, effectively reducing energy loss during the transmission process.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Additive Manufacturing Zero Thermal Expansion Lattice Structures Based on Uniform Metal Droplet 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Uniform metal droplet 3D printing allows the embedded of functional components during the printing process, which has a unique advantage in the additive manufacturing of bimetallic zero thermal expansion (ZTE) lattice structures. However, controlling the inner morphology and eliminating the hole defects within the Al/Ti connecting region is challenging. Moreover, the intermetallic compounds generated by the deposition of aluminum droplets on the titanium part surface still remain to be elucidated. This work proposes a novel method for ZTE lattice structures additive manufacturing based on uniform metal droplet 3D printing. The aluminum alloy parts were printed by uniform metal droplet 3D printing, and the titanium alloy part was embedded during the printing process to achieve the integrated fabrication of three-dimensional Al/Ti bimetallic ZTE lattices. The effect of the preheating temperature on the cold laps and lack of fusion defect were investigated. The intermetallic compounds between Al and Ti are observed by SEM images. Finally, Al/Ti bimetallic ZTE lattice structures with high-quality inner morphology were successfully printed. This paper lays the foundation for the high-quality manufacturing of bimetallic ZTE lattice structures via metal droplet 3D printing.

articleTitle: Screening and Application ofHEp-2 Cell Culture Medium without Ingredients of Animal Origin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Indirect immunofluorescence is a commonly used method for preliminary diagnosis of autoimmune diseases, which has the characteristics of simplicity and high specificity. Human laryngeal cancer cells (HEp-2 cells) are the main raw material for preparing indirect immunofluorescence detection kits. Driven by the international trend of human serum free, countries such as the United States and European Union has stopped using serum in biopharmaceuticals in 2010. Henceforth, the development of culture media serum-free, and even animal free, for HEp-2 cells is an urgent task. In the study, 4 different serum free culture media were used for adaptive culture and domestication of Hep-2 cells, pancreatin of animal original was replaced by recombinant trypsin during cell isolation, and the differences between 3 serum -free/non animal original culture media and normal serum-containing media were compared through cell counting and cell morphology. Besides, differently cultured cell sheets were used during indirect immunofluorescence test, results showed that cell doubling duration in serum 1640 culture media was 25 hours and cell doubling duration in CD-100 and OPM-AM146 culture media was 28 hours, indicating no obvious difference compared with control group cultured in serum media concerning doubling duration and proliferation curve; cell doubling duration in ToCell® Vero CD culture media was between 32-37 hours, representing a significant difference in doubling time. And there is no difference in the detection limit for known positive samples during the indirect immunofluorescence assay performed using cells cultured in the screened culture media.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Investigation of the Dynamic Response of Amplitude Modulation AFM Based on MD Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is chosen to model an amplitude modulation atomic force microscope (AM-AFM) using a point mass model to describe the vibrational mode of the cantilever tip. In the simulation, the cantilever tip responds to both tip-sample interaction and applied excitation. The simulation yields variation in the tip amplitude and phase shift with the tip-sample distance, with the results in agreement with the researcher’s experiments. An expression for the energy dissipation during the tip measurement is derived, and the results obtained from the simulation are fitted to analyze the differences between the simulation results and the actual experiments in terms of the tip size and sample thickness. The MD model of bimodal AFM is established based on the double spring double oscillator model. The reliability of the model is initially verified by the displacement response of the tip and the FFT results. The establishment of the above model can help us better understand the measurement mechanism of amplitude modulation AFM from the atomic scale aspect.

articleTitle: Preparation of Patterned Structures in Micro and Sub-0icro Scales with Superhydrophobic on Stainless Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, patterned grooving and columnar micron-submicron structures were designed and fabricated on 304 stainless steel and 316L stainless steel by laser direct writing technique. The effects of laser power, laser scanning speed and laser scanning distance on the morphology and size of the micron-submicron structures were investigated. The morphology and size of the structure were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and the surface energy of the micron-submicron structure was reduced by 1H, 1H, 2H, 2H-Perfluorodecyltrimethoxysilane (fluorosilane) ethanol solution. The effect of micro-submicron structure on the superhydrophobic properties of stainless steel surface was studied by adjusting the laser direct writing parameters. The results show that when the laser power is 10W, the laser scanning speed is 100 mm/s, and the laser scanning distance is 100 μm, the linear groove structure with super hydrophobic properties is obtained on the 304 stainless steel surface, the period is 100 μm, the minimum size is 3 μm, and the contact angle is up to 168.1°.

articleTitle: An Extra-Thick Photoresist Processing Method for Extreme Heating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As a commonly used lift-off mask for multifunctional devices fabrication, the performance of photoresist is deeply affected by temperature conditions in the subsequent process. Extra-thick photoresists often appear bubble explosion, carbonization and deformation problems after long-time and high temperature processing. This work proposed a suitable extra-thick photoresist processing method for extreme heating conditions (high temperature and long-time) to explore its performance in multi-overlay process for fabricating multi-functional devices. In addition, this work also improved the subsequent lift-off process conditions, which shortened the processing time. Above results make the extra-thick photoresist as a lift-off mask show more stable performance for subsequent processes such as electron beam evaporation, which help realize the fabrication of multifunctional devices.

articleTitle: Development of Dual Fluorescence qPCR for the Detection of Pseudomonas Aeruginosa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: To establish a real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR method for the detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), which provides an effective method for the rapid and accurate clinical detection of PA. Methods: Using the principle of fluorescence quantitative PCR technology, the relatively conserved and highly specific DNA sequences of the ETA and OPRL double genes of PA were selected as templates, primers and probes were designed by TaqMan probe method, and standard curves were constructed, so as to establish a dual fluorescence quantitative PCR system for the detection of PA. Results: Orthogonal experiments were used to optimise the reaction system and reaction conditions, and to establish a standard curve for the detection of target genes by dual fluorescence quantitative PCR; the results of specificity experiments showed that except for the two standards that showed positive results, other strains (Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus thuringiensis, etc.) showed negative results, and the method has good specificity; multiple sets of replicate assays were carried out on the positive standards for 1d and 30d, respectively, and the results showed that the method has good stability. The results showed that the stability of the method was good; the sensitivity experiments showed that the sensitivity of the method for the detection of the two positive QCs could reach 4.68×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>copies/ml and 4.54×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>copies/ml. Conclusion: Dual real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR for the detection of ETA and OPRL genes can be applied to the rapid detection of PA, which has the advantages of higher sensitivity and better specificity and stability, and has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Laser Interference Lithography of Inverse Opal Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Inverse opal structures are 3D micro-nanostructures with periodic pores, which gives them controllable photonic bandgap, high specific surface area, and excellent mechanical properties. Its manufacturing technology has attracted considerable interest. Laser interference lithography for manufacturing 3D micro-nanostructures has advantages such as high resolution, high efficiency, and high controllability. This article introduces a simulation study on 3+1 beams laser interference lithography to achieve controllable manufacturing of inverse opal structures. The modulation effects of multi-beam parameters on the pattern and scale of the light field are simulated. The results indicate that the light field exhibits a periodic intensity distribution in the X, Y, and Z directions. By modifying the incident angles of the beams, the light field period can be regulated from 0.404 μm to 23.737 μm. The azimuth angles of the beams significantly impact the pattern, period, and contrast of the light field. The combination of the beams with different polarization angles can produce various light field patterns. The initial phase variation of the beams does not affect the light field pattern, but it will cause a shift in the light field. The investigation of the light field modulation technology for 3+1 beams laser interference lithography is significant for the controllable manufacturing of inverse opal structures.

articleTitle: Study on the Detection Method of Rheumatoid Factor Based on Nano-Microspheres
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Rheumatoid factor (RF) plays an important role in clinical practice as an important indicator for detecting immunologic diseases. The aim of this study was to develop a system for the detection of rheumatoid factor (RF) using nanomicrosphere immunoturbidimetric assay (PETIA). This study will optimize the traditional method of reagent preparation by coupling small-sized microspheres to antigen to extend the linear range of the assay and adding large-sized microspheres to increase the sensitivity of the assay and make the kit more accurate. Methods: Screening (RF antigen, particle size of nano-microspheres) and determining appropriate reaction conditions, combining RF antigen with nanomicrospheres to establish PETIA detection of RF, and finally performance evaluation and analysis. RESULTS: The reagents were prepared by using RF antigen, small-size nanomicrospheres JSR-P0115 and large-size nanomicrospheres JSR-P0323 from Aoyan Bio, and the ratio of the small spheres to the large spheres was 10:1. The relative deviation of the accuracy of the method was not more than 2%; the CV value of the inter- and intra-batch precision was not more than 3%; and the linear range was from 0 to 390 mg/L, with the linear equations of y= 0.0017x + 0.0023, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.9979 > 0.99, which is better than the commercially available kits. The reagent is easy to use, with accurate results, wide linear range, good stability, low price, and can be completely used for the detection of clinical specimens.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a New Compact and Totally Decoupled Nanopositioning Stage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: MicroLED mass repair is crucial for enhancing transfer yield and reduce costs, as the precision alignment demands exceed the capabilities of traditional macro motors. In response to the problem of lacking a high-precision, compact and large-stroke positioning stage for MicroLED mass repair, this paper proposes a nanopostioning stage to compensate the accuracy of macro motors. The nanopositioning stage adopts flexible guiding mechanisms in an asymmetric structure to achieve high decoupling ratio and compact size. The static modeling of the nanopositioning stage is carried out derived from the principles of Eulerian Bernoulli beam theory and compliance modeling theory. Finite element analysis simulation and optimization with ANSYS Workbench has been performed to improve the stroke and reduce the coupling ratio. Finally, the nanopositioning stage gains large stroke in the X and Y directions, i.e., 278 μm, and low coupling rate, i.e., 0.3%.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Cutting Titanium Alloy with Micro-Textured tool
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Titanium alloy (TC4), as a typical difficult-to- machining material, greatly affects the cutting force in the process of cutting titanium alloy. This paper studied the influence of the surface texture of the turning tool on the cutting performance. The simulation model of turning titanium alloy material is established by using ABAQUS finite element simulation software, and orthogonal cutting experiments are carried out. Three kinds of micro-textured tool with different distances from the edge are designed. The study examines how the distance of texture from the edge influences the cutting capability of a micro-textured tool. The results show that when he texture distance from edge is 35um, the cutting capability of the tool is improved most obviously, relatived to the untextured tool, the cutting force decreases by 10.4%, and the shear angle increases by 5.39%. Micro-textures can induce secondary cutting, making the inner surface of the chip more smooth and smooth.

articleTitle: Switch for Magnetic Refrigeration with Surface Fabricated by Laser Inteference Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The paper examines the problem of creating an alternative solid-state magnetic cooling technology using the magnetocaloric effect in rare-earth magnetic materials. Known gas cryoculi implement the thermodynamic Stirling (Gifford-McMahon) cycle with a high temperature difference achieved, but low efficiency of the cooling process. The best solid-state materials are, in principle, capable of increasing the efficiency of the thermodynamic process. However, in order to find the ideal efficiency, in a magnetocaloric solid-state refrigerator, it is necessary to turn to the Carnot cycle and study thermal manipulation in a vacuum with high speed and negligible losses. Thus, the problem of creating a thermal switch operating in a vacuum and strong magnetic fields is of primary importance. In this work, the concept of a solid-state magnetic refrigerator with thermal interfaces in the form of a vacuum gap with a surface modified by laser interference lithography (LIL) has been developed. A method for experimental determination of contact thermal conductivity (contact thermal resistance) of unsteady heat flux in a wide temperature range from 7 K to 325 K is described. A review of micro- and nanostructured surfaces for use as thermal interfaces in electronics and cryogenic engineering is provided. The prospect of using LIL modified thermo interfaces in thermal switches is noted.

articleTitle: Effect of Ultrasonic Vibration on Micro-EDM of C/SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Ceramic matrix composites are typical difficult to process materials because of their anisotropy and hard brittleness. Aiming at the defects of existing traditional machining methods such as delamination and burr, and the problems of low forming quality in laser machining, a new ultrasonic vibration-assisted micro-EDM method was proposed to realize efficient machining of C/SiC composites by using ultrasonic cavitation and pumping. Based on micro-EDM and the introduction of ultrasonic vibration, this paper analyzes the principle of ultrasonic vibration-assisted machining of C/SiC composites, takes ultrasonic amplitude as the research object, and studies the influence of different ultrasonic amplitudes on machining efficiency, discharge stability and surface quality by observing the morphology of holes and calculating the material removal rate.

articleTitle: Periodic Silicon Metasurfaces for High Performance Structural Color
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Structural color can be divided into plasmonic structural color and all-dielectric structural color, and dielectric structural color is becoming the first choice for making structural color because of its high color saturation and low cost. In this work, a large area of silicon-based structural color was fabricated using the Taber effect based on laser interference theory from commercial silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrates on the basis of FDTD simulation. Consequently, periodic grating silicon metasurfaces with a width of 106 nm can achieve a maximum spectral reflectance of up to 91% at 650-700 nm, which can produce bright red structural color, providing a reliable way for the fabrication of low cost and high performance dielectric structural color at low cost.

articleTitle: SlipChip-Based Microfluidic Device Efficient Sample Preparation and Multiplexed PCR Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Screening for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is essential for the control and prevention of cervical cancer. While laboratory-based nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) provide precise HPV diagnosis, they generally necessitate expensive equipment, specialized laboratory facilities, and trained personnel. Combining high-quality sample preparation with rapid multiplexed detection offers substantial promise. In this study, we introduce an injection-molded SlipChip, inspired by the combination lock mechanism, that can execute magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction through a series of clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. Furthermore, we have incorporated a portable, four-channel real-time quantitative PCR device for the amplification and detection processes. This system successfully demonstrates the concurrent detection of four PCR channels for HPV screening. This innovation signifies a major step forward in HPV screening, especially for resource-limited environments, and it holds potential for broader applications in NAAT for point-of-care and home-based testing.

articleTitle: Heat Transfer Enhancement in Microchannel Heat Sink with Rectangular Diagonal Ribs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, the flow and heat transfer characteristics of a new microchannel heat sink with oblique rectangular ribs are investigated. Numerical simulations are used to compare the Nusselt number (Nu), friction factor (f), comprehensive performance factor (η), and flow profile of rectangular ribs and rectangular ribs (MC-STRB) with different microchannels: 30° (MC-THRB), 45° (MC-FORB), 60° (MC-SIRB), and smooth microchannels (MC-SH). The results show that this new inclined rectangular rib can increase the vortex flow in the microchannel radiator, make the stagnant zone in the flow channel smaller, and significantly improve the heat transfer effect of the microchannel radiator. In addition, the microchannels with inclined rectangular ribs at an angle of 60° have the optimal comprehensive performance in all cases, with a comprehensive performance factor of 1.33 at Re=800.

articleTitle: PGC-Arctan Demodulation Method Based on Improved IKEF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The proposed method is an improvement on the traditional PGC demodulation technique, specifically addressing the impact of carrier phase delay, modulation depth drift, and low-frequency ambient noise on phase demodulation accuracy in phase-modulated homodyne interferometers. It utilises an improved iterative extended Kalman filtering (IEKF) approach. The algorithm enhances the iterative updating process by incorporating a damping factor into the traditional IEKF. This enables optimal estimation and correction of the parameters of the PGC quadrature signals, resulting in reduced nonlinear error in the demodulation process. Additionally, the improved algorithm achieves higher demodulation accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate the method's effectiveness in eliminating nonlinear error in phase generation carrier.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Enhancing Contour Features of Tissue Cell Images Based on Fluorescence in Situ Hybridization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the widespread application of computer technology in medical image processing, preprocessing fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) tissue cell images with complex structures to obtain clear contour features is crucial to ensure the effectiveness of artificial intelligence models. Clear image contour features directly affect the performance of artificial intelligence models. Therefore, in-depth research was conducted on how to enhance the contour feature information of complex FISH tissue cell images, and improvements were made based on existing algorithms. An image contour enhancement method combining image illumination and an improved local binary pattern (LBP) algorithm is proposed. This method uses an illumination enhancement algorithm to improve the overall distribution of image brightness, and then uses an improved local binary pattern algorithm to quickly extract the contour features of the image, and weights the extracted features into the illumination-enhanced image to obtain an image with enhanced contour features. Finally, areas with high energy gradients are identified through piecewise linear functions and heat maps, which effectively filter out areas with low energy gradients. The high-frequency signal areas are the outline areas of FISH tissue cell images. Experimental analysis verified the effectiveness of this method in image enhancement.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Glass Micro/Nano Array Mirrors via Continuous Laser Direct Irradiation Assisted by Microperforated Masking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper introduces a process that combines continuous laser direct writing and mask techniques to fabricate micro/nanoscale array microlenses on K9 glass. Initially, a zirconia ceramic mask with an array of holes was prepared using laser-assisted mechanical drilling. Subsequently, by precisely controlling continuous laser scanning through the designated microholes to irradiate the glass, optical microlenses were formed on the glass surface. Through simulation, we investigated the influence of laser parameters on the shape of the resulting optical microlenses. We found that the width and height of the microlenses were positively correlated with laser power and negatively correlated with laser radius. We then experimentally fabricated micro/nanoscale glass array lenses and validated the accuracy of the simulation model by comparing the simulation data with experimental measurements. Finally, we established a dimensionless predictive model through numerical fitting, which correlates lens shape with laser parameters. The results demonstrate that our proposed method can effectively produce micro/nanoscale glass array lenses suitable for mass production of optical microarray lenses, thus providing a novel approach for fabricating micro/nano optical devices.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electrical Performance of Short-Channel MoS2 Transistors through Dual-Gate Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has significant potential for future electronic devices. As transistor sizes shrink, conventional top-gate MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistors exhibit deteriorating direct current (DC) performance under short-channel conditions. This paper proposes improving the DC performance of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistors under short channel by introducing a local bottom-gate to form a dual-gate structure. Simulation studies show that dual-gate structure transistors offer advantages such as low off-state current, small subthreshold swing (SS), high on/off ratio, and large transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>). In addition, our analysis of the MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistors' radio frequency (RF) performance reveals that under sub-50 nm gate lengths, both dual-gate and top-gate structures achieve comparable cut-off frequencies (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) and maximum oscillation frequencies (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>), both exceeding 100 GHz. By comprehensively analyzing the DC and RF properties of dual-gate and top-gate MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> transistors, we identify parasitic capacitance as a key factor hindering the improvement of RF performance in dual-gate structures. These results demonstrate the potential of dual-gate structures in future high-performance short-channel transistor applications.

articleTitle: Stability Study of Leukocyte Differentiation Antigen CD34 (Flow Cytometry-PE) Detection Kit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The Leukocyte Differentiation Antigen CD34 Detection Kit (Flow Cytometry-PE) is an in vitro diagnostic tool that can identify the expression level of CD34 antigen in human bone marrow cells, aiding in the diagnosis of hematological tumors. This paper conducts real-time stability, transport stability, open stability, high-temperature accelerated degradation stability experiments on three batches of detection kits, testing appearance, accuracy, precision, and performing staining stability experiments to evaluate the stability of the kit. The results show that the kit is stable when stored at 4°C for 24 months, transported at 4°C for 7 days, opened for 18 months, and incubated at 37 °C in the dark for 4 weeks. Additionally, samples can be stored at 4°C in the dark for 48 hours before staining and 24 hours after staining. The experimental results provide guidance and reference for the development of the Leukocyte Differentiation Antigen CD34 Detection Kit.

articleTitle: Design and Experiments of a Non-Resonant Hollow Vibration Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The design and characteristic analysis of a novel non-resonant hollow vibration generator are introduced in this paper. The hollow vibration generator is developed based on the stacked ring PZT actuator and compliant mechanism. Finite element analysis is carried out to characterize its static and dynamic performance. A prototyped non-resonant hollow vibration generator is fabricated, followed by a series of experimental investigations to thoroughly assess its performance and characteristics. The results show that the natural frequency of the hollow vibration generator is 6.37 kHz. The vibration amplitude and frequency are proved to be independently tunable to meet different requirements of vibration parameters.

articleTitle: Methodological Establishment of ACR Chromatographic Assay in Urine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: Urine ACR is the ratio of urinary microalbumin to creatinine, and its clinical significance is to determine early kidney injury, which is an important indicator reflecting kidney function. In this paper, two routine indicators in human urine, microalbumin and creatinine, were detected by urine dry chemistry analyser, and the optimization of microalbumin as well as creatinine dry chemistry test strips made their test results more accurate and stable. Then, through the comparative testing of dry chemistry urine analyser and biochemistry analyser, it shows that dry chemistry urine analyser is simple to operate, more rapid and higher performance, and has low cost, so it is carried out to innovate the methodology of ACR.

articleTitle: Research of AFM Image Matching Based on Wavelet Transform SIFT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Atomic force microscopy is a valuable tool for assessing the surface morphology and mechanical properties of dynamic biological processes. However, the inevitable presence of noise in the image data makes it difficult to accurately capture a wide range of microscopic changes. In this study, we developed an optimization method based on the wavelet transform to effectively remove residual noise from image data while retaining the information necessary to describe image characteristics. The optimized results demonstrate that the scale-invariant feature transform matching algorithm significantly enhances imaging efficiency and broadens the detection range.

articleTitle: Research on AZ91D Magnesium Alloy Self-Healing Coating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Magnesium (Mg) alloys have a lot of unique properties, but poor corrosion resistance. Effective anti-corrosion strategies are necessary for the wide application of magnesium alloys. At present, the common surface treatment technologies of magnesium alloy include chemical conversion film, anodic oxidation, plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO), electroplating, and electroless plating. However, many films will lose their protective ability and even accelerate the corrosion of the magnesium matrix after being damaged, which greatly reduces the service life of the film. In this study, we developed a corrosion-resistant composite coating for magnesium alloys with inherent self-healing properties. To effectively protect magnesium alloys, we integrated laser processing with hydrothermal reactions, followed by immersion in a manganese chloride solution, to create a self-healing coating that not only resists corrosion but also forms new substances. Even if the sample is soaked in 0.9wt%Nacl solution after the scratch test, a new substance can be produced on the surface of the sample, which covers the scratch area layer by layer and maintains excellent anti-corrosion performance. This is because during the corrosion process, the newly formed substance reacts spontaneously with the bivalent magnesium ions and hydroxide radicals generated during the corrosion process, and the newly formed substance is the magnesium manganese bilayer hydroxide. Therefore, we believe that the prepared composite coating can effectively prevent the spread of corrosive substances, enhance the corrosion resistance of the sample surface, and offer durable and effective protection. Moreover, this method has the advantages of simple preparation and low cost, so we believe that this strategy will give a new idea for the design of new anti-corrosion coatings.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Dynamics of the Carrier in InP/ZnS Core-Shell Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As the typical fluorescent semiconductor quantum dots, the InP/ZnS core-shell quantum dots exhibit excellent performances in energy, optoelectronic, catalysis and other fields. The carrier is closely related to adjust the photoelectric properties of the materials, hence, understanding the dynamics of the carrier in InP/ZnS quantum dots is important for broadening its application prospects. Here, the photoinduced carrier dynamics in InP/ZnS quantum dots was studied through the femtosecond pump-probe transient absorption spectroscopy. The carrier relaxation processes consisted of the hole states trapping, the defect states capture and the carrier radiative recombination. Our work provided a useful reference to design and fabricate the higher photoelectric efficiency core-shell quantum dots.

articleTitle: High-Quality and Efficiency Machining of Micro-EDM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Machining electrode wear is unavoidable in micro-EDM, especially for complex three-dimensional cavity or microgroove. Tool electrodes not only have axial wear that affects the machining depth, but also have radial wear that leads to inconsistency in width before and after machining, thus affecting the machining accuracy. In this paper, the multi-performance parameter optimization method of micro-EDM based on grey relational analysis (GRA) is proposed to reduce the machining time and reduce the electrode wear by taking the machining time, axial and radial electrode wear during microgroove machining as evaluation indicators. Through the orthogonal experiment results, the grey relational grade of multi-performance parameter is calculated and ranked, and the group with the greatest grey relational grade of the orthogonal experiment is obtained as 17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> group. Compared by 17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> orthogonal experiment, the results of the optimal experiment that the machining time, axial and radical electrode wear are respectively reduced by 13.89%, 3.31%, and 10.80%, which have achieved high efficiency and low electrode wear in micro-EDM.

articleTitle: A Cell Microscopy Image Recognition Method Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning cell recognition algorithm based on an improved Inception-V3 model. The algorithm first preprocesses the images and creates a dataset. Then, it modifies the Inception-V3 model by adding and improving layers to retain more local detail information and extract more effective features. Finally, the improved network is used to train the model and conduct experiments. The experimental results show that the performance of the improved model is approximately 5% better than that of the original model.

articleTitle: Optimization of Shark Groove Drag Reduction Based on CFD and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: An optimization of shark scale flake groove structure by genetic algorithm is proposed to enhance its drag reduction performance. The microstructure of shark scales has been shown to play a key role in reducing frictional drag and enhancing hydrodynamic efficiency. Therefore, a genetic algorithm was used to optimize the design of the groove shape of the scales to exhibit optimal performance in the fluid environment. Genetic algorithms of selection, crossover and mutation are used to find the optimal solution in the design space. The optimized design is validated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) technique. The CFD simulation results demonstrate the improved hydrodynamic performance of the optimized groove design and confirm the effectiveness of genetic algorithms in complex engineering design problems. This study provides a new research avenue to improve the hydrodynamic efficiency.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Vibration-Enhanced Liquid Precursor Filling in Porous Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The filling and curing of liquid precursor in porous templates is a common method to construct functional materials with nanostructures, such as advanced electrodes and actuators. However, the filling of liquid precursors, especially those with high viscosity, in micro/nano structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a strategy to enhance the filling of liquid precursor in porous nanostructures by using three-dimensional vibration assistance. We numerically simulate the filling effects of different frequencies and amplitudes of the vibration without introducing complex energy fields. To simplify the computational model and enhance convergence, a numerical model is established under a two-dimensional physical field. The results indicate that the filling depth can be obviously enhanced by vibration assistance. Compared with the filling without external assistance, the introduction of horizontal vibration at frequency of 600 Hz and amplitude of 400 nm enables the filling rate to be increased by 102%, while the vertical vibration at frequency of 500 Hz and amplitude of 200 nm results in an increase of filling rates by 160%. Under the optimal parameters, the coupled 3D oscillations enables complete fluid domain filling in the computational model. The proposed method holds promise for enhancing the filling rates of high viscosity solutions and reducing filling defects in porous nanostructures, demonstrating its excellent practical value in the fabrication of nano-devices through templating methods.

articleTitle: Research Progress in Micro-Nano Optometry and Ophthalmology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Existing interventions that slow myopia progression has limited the effectiveness and some side effects. Repeated low-level red-light (RLRL), as a new method for the myopia treatment, has become a research topic in the myopia treatment in recent years. To explore the application potential of RLRL therapy for controlling myopia progression, the cellular and molecular mechanisms of RLRL therapy urgently need further investigation. Therefore, in this paper, we review the red-light irradiation intervention and control of myopia progression from the perspective of micro-nano optometry and ophthalmology, aiming to provide a reference for preventing and treating of myopia.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Optimization of MEMS Gas Sensor Microhotplate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The gas sensor microhotplate, as a key component of the gas sensor, is of great significance for improving the energy utilization and gas-sensitive performance of the gas sensor. The MEMS gas sensor microhotplate designed in this paper adopts the suspended-film structure, proposes novel shapes of electrode, and applies finite element technology to conduct multi-physical field coupling modeling and simulation, and compares and analyzes the temperature and stress distributions as well as the power consumption of each plan, and selects the optimal plan for the structural optimization work. Finally, based on the established model of the microhotplate, an optimization model is built by using COMSOL. After optimization, the temperature gradient of the microhotplate is reduced from 15.6% to 6.6%, and only 9.14 mW is needed to reach 390°C, which achieves the improvement of the heating performance of the MEMS gas sensor microhotplate.

articleTitle: Friction Behavior of Graphite/h-BN Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and an improved PT model (phononic friction model), we observed not only regular atomic-scale friction force but also complex stick-slip phenomenon at the moiré-scale on graphene/h-BN heterostructures. Furthermore, on the superlattices of graphene/h-BN heterostructures, we found that the friction behavior of nanotip sliding is strongly modulated by the moiré superlattices. This modulation is evident not only in the stick-slip behavior of instantaneous friction force but also in the trend of average friction force with velocity. Through the phononic friction model, we demonstrated that due to the relative motion between the nanotip and the substrate, an excess of phonons is excited at the washboard frequency. This leads to resonance in the nanotip and results in peaks in the average friction force. This work reveals the moiré period dependence of friction behavior in heterostructures, offering a novel approach to controlling the friction force of graphene/h-BN superlattice structures.

articleTitle: Employing Optimized Anode to Improve Bubble Accumulation in Localized Electrochemical Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of localized electrochemical deposition (LECD) technology, the bubbles generated during the deposition process have become an important influence limiting the molding of microstructures. High-quality metal microstructures have a wide range of applications in microelectronics, biomedicine, and micro sensors. In this study, the effect of whether the anode tip is exposed or not on the electrolyte potential distribution is explored through simulation, and the anode is optimized to enable the rapid escape of tiny bubbles in the form of bubble streams to avoid the formation of localized air holes between the microanode and cathode substrate caused by the clogging of large bubbles. The fabrication of optimized anode has the advantages of simple process, low cost and short fabrication period, and the use of optimized anode can avoid the formation of tiny air pockets, promote the liquid-phase mass transfer in the process of LECD and improve the quality of the deposited microstructures, which has a good use value and a wide range of application prospects for the improvement of the LECD process.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer Based Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Fast Tool Servo System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The piezo-driven Fast tool servo (FTS) is a kind of ultra-precision machining technology. For the uncertainty of the system and the parameter changes caused by dynamic machining loads, a disturbance observer (DOB) based an adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) strategy is proposed for the piezo-driven FTS system. By treating the effects of hysteresis nonlinearities, model uncertainties, cutting load, and external disturbances, a DOB is initially designed to estimate and compensate for this combined disturbance. Building on the DOB framework, a sliding mode controller with a PID surface is then introduced for the FTS. We prove the stability of the control system by using Lyapunov theory. The effectiveness of the proposed DOB-based ADSMC method is validated through experiments on a piezo-driven FTS prototype, showcasing significant improvements in tracking performance, disturbance rejection, and robustness against system variations compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Resonance Frequency Tuning of Piezoresistive Cantilever Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Recent results in development of a new method for real-time detection of ultra-small objects such as pathogens and/or biomarkers in air with piezoresistive microcantilevers, are summarized. In order to achieve as low detection limit as 10 fg with "large-size" cantilevers, a concept exploiting arrays of active and reference cantilevers which possess incrementally increased resonance frequencies, is proposed. To ensure reproducible operation of the prototypes a method for fine tuning of cantilevers' resonance frequencies, is developed. Based on results of computer simulations the impact of specific laser micromachining on tuning the parameters, was studied. The obtained results and future research objectives are discussed.

articleTitle: Study on the Preparation and the Degradation of Congo Red Dye Performance of La, Ce-Mn Composite Oxides
