publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this study, La, Ce-Mn series rare earth composite oxides were synthesized and characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV-Vis spectroscopy, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR). The degradation efficiency of these composite oxides on Congo red dye was investigated. Experimental results indicated that Ce-Mn and La+Ce-Mn composite oxides exhibited excellent catalytic activation of potassium peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for the degradation of Congo red dye, achieving a degradation efficiency of over 99%. The high efficiency of the composite oxides was primarily attributed to the active species, with the main contributor being electron holes (h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>), followed by superoxide radicals (ЬO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup>) and hydroxyl radicals (ЬOH). These active species play a crucial role in the oxidative degradation of organic pollutants.

articleTitle: Bioinspired Reverse Coupling Architecture for Streamlined Droplet Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Micro/nano structured surfaces with patterned wettability have garnered widespread attention across various fields, such as aerospace and energy storage, due to their unique functionalities. However, the unidirectional driving constraint has limited the construction of complex-shaped droplets. In this study, we synergistically mimicked the asymmetrical structures of pine needles and duck bills, coupling them inversely to design a novel driving platform for streamlined droplet formation. To meet the demands of functional structural design, the biomimetic platform comprises two parts: a transport substrate and embedded protrusions. The fabrication method adopts 3D printing. After hydrocholoric acid etching to create a micro-nanostructure, the platform's surface is coated with a fluorinated polydimethylsiloxane (F-PDMS) solution to achieve low surface energy and differential super-wettability. Using experimental and simulation analyses, we investigated the impact of the narrow-end spacing of the embedded protrusions, coupling angle, and wedge angle on the cross-sectional length, height, and contour uniformity of the resultant streamlined droplets. Results revealed the driving mechanism for bidirectional droplet transport.

articleTitle: Polarization Surface Relief Gratings Coupled with Diffractive Waveguide for Near-Eye Display
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper proposes a polarization surface relief grating (PSRG) coupling device for diffractive waveguide display. The rectangular tilted grating is taken as the object of study, and the grating structure parameters under the best performance are given. The design results demonstrate that when in different TE and TM modes, the diffraction efficiency of the two is the same and is above 92%. The working conditions and manufacturing errors are not only insensitive to the impact of the structure but also to meeting the feasibility of the processing, and still have a broad wavelength and angular response bandwidth. This is significant for the field-of-view (FOV) extension and full-colour display of holographic waveguide display systems.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Meso-Butanediol Dehydrogenase in Comamonas testosteroni ATCC11996
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Comamonas testosteroni is a steroid hormones degradation bacterium and it is also an opportunistic pathogen can cause bacteremia in human. In this work, a MBD gene was knocked out in C. testosteroni ATCC11996 which was up regulated induced with testosterone in transcriptome, obtained a MBD gene knocked out mutant. The gene was cloned, overexpressed, and prepared MBD polyclonal antibody. Compared the wild type and gene knockout mutant strains degradation ability for testosterone, methyltestosterone, estrone and 17α-ethynylestradiol by HPLC. Detected MBD protein expression level with different regulator LuxR, LysR and TetR by ELISA. All of these results were shown that the molecular weight of MBD overexpression was 28.12 kDa, the testosterone degradation ability of the gene knockout mutant has significantly decreased of 47.4%, the MBD protein expression in wild type strain was obviously increased after testosterone induced. These results support that MBD should be involved in testosterone degradation in C testosteroni ATCC11996. Moreover, LuxR regulator should be a repressor for MBD expression under testosterone induction. This study provides a basis for further understanding the steroids degradation in C. testosteroni ATCC11996 and the metabolic reactions caused by this opportunistic pathogen in human.

articleTitle: Mechanical Structure Design of Microdrop Digital PCR Chip Reader
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The application of digital PCR technology in the field of biomedicine has become an important molecular biological analysis method. Microdrop digital PCR chip reader is a key component of digital PCR system, and its mechanical structure design plays a crucial role in the performance and function of the device. In order to improve the accuracy, stability and efficiency of the microdrop digital PCR chip reader, the key elements and principles of its mechanical structure design are discussed. Firstly, the working principle, design tasks and objectives of the microdrop digital PCR chip reader are analyzed. Secondly, the key components of the mechanical structure design, such as chip positioning structure, chip tray movement system structure, switching filter structure and optical system mechanical structure, are discussed in detail. Finally, through the simulation analysis, the feasibility and superiority of the design scheme are verified, which provides a reliable theoretical basis and practical guidance for the mechanical structure design of the microdrop digital PCR chip reader.

articleTitle: Preparation and Optical Performance of Polyimide Thin Films with Micro Prism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In response to the problem of high indoor temperature caused by direct sunlight, this work prepared polyimide films with micro prism structures. Compared to unstructured PI films, the PI micro prism film exhibits excellent reflection efficiency in the visible light region (400 nm-800 nm), with the highest reflectivity reaching 38.25% at a period of 13 pm. In addition, in the infrared band (8-14 μ m), both PI microprisms and PI films exhibit good radiative cooling performance. PI micro prism thin film has good potential in reducing room temperature when applied to indoor glass surfaces.

Author Keywords: polyimide thin films with micro prism

articleTitle: Expression and Characterisation of Pyrophosphatase TK1700 from Thermus Thermophilus Archaea
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: An inorganic pyrophosphatase gene (TK1700) from the thermophilic archaea Thermococcus kodakarensis was cloned on the plas mid pET-28a and successfully expressed in the Escherichia coli strain BL21 (DE3). The activity characterization of purified recombinant TK1700 pyrophospha tase after purification showed that recombinant pyrophosphatase TK1700 showed the highest catalytic activity at 50 °C-60 °C, and the optimal pH range was narrow (7-9), which was a neutral pyrophosphatase. When pyrophosphatase TK1700 was added to thermal cycle PCR, the PCR reaction could amplify more products under the high concentration of PPi. In this experiment, a new inorganic pyrophosphatase was obtained and could be appied as a new PCR enhancer to improve PCR performance.

articleTitle: Research on Low-Loss Flow Detection Method Based on Pressure Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To reduce sample loss and lower the cost of flow cytometry experiments, a detection method based on sheath pressure feedback is proposed. By identifying the dramatic pressure fluctuations caused by the air cushion, the time when the sample reaches the detection area can be accurately located, thereby minimizing the volume of discarded samples. The experimental platform was built to test the forward scatter signals and the particle detection time of quality control microspheres, which were used to determine the key parameters of the experiment. In the experiment, we used the suspension of 900 nm diameter polystyrene microspheres as a sample, and set different detection volumes and sample flow rates. We confirmed that when the sample flow rate was in the range of 5-50 μl/min, the volume to be measured was in the range of 10-50 μl. The detection method could effectively reduce the sample loss to less than 5 μl.

articleTitle: Model Analysis of the Gear Box of the Electromechanical Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The electromechanical transmission system has emerged as the dominant type of transmission in the heavy vehicle field. In this research, a finite element model is established for the gear box of the electromechanical transmission system. It can be revealed the inherent characteristics of the electromechanical transmission system by analyzing the 10 modal frequencies and vibration modes under three different constraints, which can provide robust support for its integrated and high-speed development.

articleTitle: The Effect of Measurement Parameters on Cellular Mechanics Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is an advanced nanotechnology that can image and measure the mechanical properties of living cells in liquid environment. However, the measurement parameters will affect the mechanics data. In this work, the effects of indentation force, indentation speed, lifting height, and probe shape on the cellular mechanics detection were studied. The results showed that the indentation depth increased alongside the indentation force, while the baseline separation distance also showed an increase corresponding to the higher indentation speed, and the lifting height and cantilever shape had a significant effect on the force curves measurements. This is important for studying the measurement of cellular mechanical properties at the nanoscale.

articleTitle: Establishment and Optimization of Quantum Dot Detection Method for Allergen-Specific IgE Antibodies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study establishes a detection method for allergen-specific IgE antibodies based on fluorescence quantum dot immunochromatography and optimizes the detection system. The optimal parameters for the conjugation of quantum dots and antibodies are quantum dots with a 120 nm diameter, activator dosages of 10 μL NHS and 5 μL EDC; specific marking antibody parameters for anti-human IgE antibodies: MES buffer (0.02 M), pH 6.0, labeled protein dosage of 10 μg, and quantum dot microsphere dosage of 25 μL. Clinical comparison validation shows high consistency, The test kit designed using this system demonstrated greater convenience, lower cost, faster detection speed, and higher portability compared to traditional instrument-based detection methods, indicating the accuracy and practicality of this detection system.

articleTitle: Fluorescence Feature Image: Fluorescence Enhancement Method Based on Illumination Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous development of computer technology in the field of molecular diagnosis, deep learning has shown great potential in enhancing fluorescence features in fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) images, allowing researchers to observe fluorescence distribution and abnormalities more clearly. Condition. of genetic material. Health status. Improves observation clarity and overall image quality of genetic material. However, due to problems such as uneven dyeing and lighting differences, the model training and generalization capabilities of deep learning are limited, thus affecting the feature recognition and accuracy of the algorithm. This method is approached from the perspective of image enhancement and feature recognition. By dynamically adjusting the lighting factors of the image to match the actual lighting distribution, this adjustment helps reduce the impact of lighting changes and makes the brightness of the image more uniform. At the same time, this method uses heat maps to quickly locate high-intensity signal areas in the image, that is, the parts with the most obvious fluorescence signals. By calculating 16 environments around these areas. Combined with the linear segmentation strategy and dynamically adjusting processing parameters, it not only highlights and enhances the clarity of image details, but also obtains accurate enhanced images. To avoid excessive enhancement of fluorescence characteristics, the fluorescence characteristics are compensated through the Cycle-Gan network to obtain the final compensation result. Finally, the effect of this method in image enhancement was verified through experimental analysis.

articleTitle: Research on the Controllable Growth of Gold Nanopillars by Nanohole Templates on Gold-Plated Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This article proposes a novel method for preparing gold nanopillars by immersing nanohole templates in reaction solutions to obtain gold nanopillars of different shapes, and explains the formation mechanism of gold nanopillars. In this work, nanohole arrays of different sizes were prepared by electron beam lithography (EBL) on gold-plated silicon substrate and silicon substrate. By immersing the nanohole template in reaction solution consisting of sodium citrate and chloroauric acid, the gold nanopillars would be obtained in the nanohole arrays. The results showed that the mushroom-shaped gold nanopillars were obtained on the template of the gold-plated substrate, while the rod-shaped gold nanopillars were obtained on the template of the silicon substrate (out of gold-plated) and the formation of the rod-shaped gold nanopillars were related to the diameter of the nanoholes. The above phenomena were analyzed from the perspective of heterogeneous nucleation site, and the morphology and composition were studied by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS).

articleTitle: Study on the Adsorption Mechanism of 2,4-D Molecules on the Surface of Cu Rectangular Structures: A Molecular Dynamics Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As a widely utilized herbicide, 2,4-D has been extensively employed on a global scale. However, its widespread utilization raises concerns regarding its environmental impact and potential health hazards. The adsorption mechanism of 2,4-D molecules on Cu substrate surfaces was investigated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The attention was focused on effect of surface morphology on the adsorption efficacy of 2,4-D. In order to investigate the adsorption process of 2,4-D molecules on rectangular grooves, an analysis was conducted on the distribution of surface 2,4-D molecules, the number of atoms within the grooves, density distribution, and the centroid positions. The findings shows the variation in both the width and depth of the rectangular grooves on the Cu substrate significantly impacts the adsorption effectiveness of 2,4-D molecules. Increasing the width allows for the 2,4-D molecules to spread over a larger surface area, while enlarging the depth facilitates more 2,4-D molecules to enter the grooves, resulting in a smaller horizontal distribution area and a predominant concentration in the vertical direction. Additionally, it was observed that the 2,4-D molecules are distributed on the surface of the substrate in a layered structure. The distribution of 2,4-D molecules on the substrate surface is divided into three layers. The density of 2,4-D distribution is greater in the lower layers, correlating with a higher number of distribution. The width and depth of the rectangular groove structure on the substrate have an impact on the distribution of the 2,4-D molecular layers. As the groove depth and width increase, the 2,4-D molecules come closer to the surface, resulting in a better surface adsorption effect.

articleTitle: Coupled Effects of Temperature and Defects on the Mechanical Properties of 8-16-4 Graphyne: Atomistic Aspect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The 8-16-4 graphyne is a freshly discovered two-dimensional carbon allotrope that exhibits unique mechanical, electrical, and adsorption properties, with potential applications in single-atom catalysis, hydrogen storage, and flexible electronic devices. This research aims to deepen our understanding of the fracture behavior and mechanical characteristics of 8-16-4 graphyne monolayers. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we investigated how temperature, along with the interactions between temperature, vacancy defects, and microcracks, influences its mechanical performance. The results indicate that 8-16-4 graphyne fractures by the cleavage of ethylene bonds at a critical strain of approximately 0.29. The mechanical properties are significantly influenced by temperature, vacancy concentration, and microcrack presence. Compared to its sibling carbon allotropes, 8-16-4 graphyne shows reduced sensitivity to vacancy defects. Pre-existing microcracks alter its fracture modes.

articleTitle: Micro-Nano Structured Laser-Induced Graphene Antibacterial Surfaces Fabricated by Two-Step Laser Marking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Graphene, with its high electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, specific surface area and easy functionalization, has shown unique advantages in antibacterial and antiviral surface applications. However, the traditional graphene preparation process is complex. In this paper, a method for preparing micro-nano structured laser-induced graphene (MLIG) antimicrobial surfaces was proposed by two-step laser ablation of polyimide (PI) films. The method is simple and efficient, and the feature size of micro-nano structures is controllable. The fabricated micro-patterned laser induced graphene(LIG) has high surface purity, stable surface properties, large porosity and superhydrophobicity. The antibacterial ability of LIG and MLIG against Staphylococcus aureus was measured by plate counting method, and the inhibitory effect of MLIG on the virus was confirmed. At the same time, the superhydrophobic MLIG surface also can enhance the self-cleaning properties of the surface and reduces the adhesion of microorganisms.

articleTitle: Adhesion Force Modeling of Octopus-like Stamp for Micro Transfer Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the rapid advancement in flexible electronics, the micro transfer printing technology is emerging as a highly promising approach for integrating micro/nano-scale heterogeneous materials in this field. A crucial aspect of micro transfer printing research revolves around studying the stamp’s controllable adhesion force, which serves as the execution device for the printing process, so it is necessary to establish an accurate adhesion force model of the stamp. In this study, we have developed a groundbreaking octopus-inspired stamp featuring both cavity and micro-channels. The adhesive force exhibited by the developed stamp arises from the combined effects of van der Waals forces at the stamp's end face and an additional adhesion force resulting from the pressure differential between the cavity and the surrounding atmosphere. The additional adhesion force of the stamp is modeled based on the fundamental principles of fluid dynamics, specifically the Navier-Stokes equation, and the first law of thermodynamics. The numerical computation of adhesion force is carried out by numerical iterative algorithm, and the effects of stretching distance and velocity on the additional adhesion force of the stamp are investigated. The numerical computation results show that the additional adhesion force of the stamp can be controlled by both the stretching distance and stretching velocity. This finding opens up new avenues for optimizing the design of octopus-like stamps used in micro transfer printing.

articleTitle: Dynamic Wetting Behavior of Femtosecond Laser-Textured Chromium Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper investigates the temporal evolution of wettability on nanostructured chromium surfaces created via Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS) using a femtosecond pulsed laser. Employing two distinct laser processing conditions, we explore their influence on surface roughness and oxidation and their correlation with changes in wettability. The study further investigates the impact of a CO2 stream on surface properties during laser processing, including its effects on the redeposition of nanoparticles derived from the laser processing and the deposition of carbon contaminants. Additionally, it investigates how storing the samples in an inert atmosphere to reduce oxidation and contamination influences wettability. The samples utilized in this study consisted of a multi-layered ABS base coated with Cu, Ni, and a superficial thin chromium layer of 200nm. These samples were laser processed to generate LIPSS without compromising the integrity of the chromium layer.Results indicate that laser processing parameters significantly affect surface roughness and oxidation and their correlation with changes in the contact angle. Storage in an inert atmosphere demonstrated to limit re-oxidation, highlighting the difference in the degree of oxidation achieved based on the laser parameters. Additionally, it has been verified that environmental carbonaceous contaminants have a significant impact on the kinetic evolution of the contact angles. This comprehensive analysis demonstrates the interaction between laser-induced surface nanostructures, environmental factors, and their collective impact on surface wettability.

articleTitle: Surface Integrity Analysis of Electrochemical Machining of TC4 Titanium Alloy and 304 Stainless Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Surface integrity determines the life and part performance of the machined part, and the study of surface integrity is very important in electrochemical machining (ECM). Therefore, this paper investigates the surface microscopic characteristics of ECM of two different characteristic materials, TC4 titanium alloy and 304 stainless steel, at three voltages. The experimental results show that: at low voltage, each of the two materials presents a unique morphology, and the machined surface of the sample piece has electrolytic products and localized stray corrosion, which worsens the quality of the machined surface. However, at high voltages, both materials present smooth and flat machined surfaces. With the increase of voltage, the surface roughness of both materials decreases gradually and reaches the lowest value when the voltage is at 20 V. The surface roughness of TC4 titanium alloy is Ra=1.55 μm; the surface roughness of 304 stainless steel is Ra=0.18 μm.

articleTitle: A Fast-Response and Sensitive Gas Sensor Based on Graphene-Tin Dioxide Film for Ammonia Detection at Ambient Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Tin dioxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is recognized for its remarkable chemical stability, thermal stability and high electron mobility, making is a suitable material for detecting ammonia gas (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>). However, SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is stability and sensitive to NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> only at high temperatures and is affected by environment conditions. This paper proposes a graphene-SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (G-S) composited film as a sensing material, enabling sensitive detection of NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at ambient temperature. The G-S gas sensor demonstrates fast-response and high stability, and enhanced sensitivity with lower detection limits. Regression analysis equations shows a strong linear correlation between gas concentration and sensor responses. Experimental results indicate that G-S gas sensor maintains detection limit down to 5 ppm NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at 25℃, resolution down to 2.6 Ω/ppm and response time as low as 40 s with repeat manners. This work presents a fast-response and stable NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gas sensor for wearable applications in daily life.

articleTitle: Performance Verification for Leukocyte Differentiation Antigen CD34 Assay Kit by Flow Cytometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this work, a performance validation of the leukocyte differentiation antigen CD34 assay kit was carried out with Kasumi-1 and SHI-1 act as positive and negative cells for CD34 by Cytek® Northern Lights-CLC flow cytometry system. The CD34 phycoerythrin (PE) assay kit reagent stained the different concentration of Kasumi-1 cells and SHI-1 cells mixture, the results shown that the concentration of CD34 positive cells in the rang 30-3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>count/μL were linear with percentage of positive cells. The precision coefficient of variation (CV) for the CD34 detection kit was less than 8% with intra-batch, inter-day, intra and inter operation monitoring detection. The correlation equation of accuracy was that Y=0.9969X+0.1566, r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>≥0.95 and there was no significant difference in t-test (p>0.05). For the specific detection, CD34 detection kit could be used in hematopoietic stem cells detection and non-reactivity to mature lymphocytes and myeloid cells. In addition, hemolysis and high-fat in samples has no significant effect on this kit detection.

articleTitle: Scanning Laser Interference Method and System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To challenges of large area, high efficiency, and low cost in laser manufacturing on micro- and nano-scale, scanning laser interference technique were proposed to manufacture micro and nano structures, combining with a high speed scanner and laser interference system. Simultaneously, developing the system’s host computer. Experiments were carried out by spin-coated photosensitive resin on quartz glass and crystalline silicon wafers at different scanning speeds, verifying the feasibility of the system for manufacturing the micro- and nano- structures at high speed and large area. In addition, the arbitrary patterns can be also explored in this system. The results demonstrated that perfectly micro structures with a period of 1.5 μm could be achieved by this system. While photosensitive resin was cured by a wavelength of 360 nm with a laser power of 5.5 mW at a scanning speed of 30 mm/s. And that the actual period was consistent with the theoretical period. Furthermore, the cured large-area micro structures also exhibited distinct structural colors. By curing Chinese characters, the system also demonstrated the feasibility for arbitrary pattern. In summary, the scanning laser interference technique were proposed to face the need of the large area, high speed, and arbitrary in micro-and nano- structures in this article. It will advance the pace of commercialization in laser micro-and nano- manufacturing.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Hydrophobic Copper Surface Using Nanosecond Laser Interference Patterning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Micro- and nano-scale surface structures are closely related to their properties, functions and applications. Herein, the hydrophobic copper (Cu) surface was fabricated using nanosecond laser interference patterning. Scanning electron microscopy images shows that the obtained Cu surface is a three-dimensional porous structure containing dimples and voids. Wherein the dimples and the voids have the ability to capture air to form an air cushion that effectively prevents water droplets from infiltrating into the surface, thereby rendering the surface hydrophobic. In addition, the wettability results display that the obtained Cu surface could reach around 107°, indicating that the Cu surface fabricated in this work is a hydrophobic material with a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of the Elliptic Vibration Shape and Frequency on the Electrochemical Micromachining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel elliptic vibration assisted wire electrochemical micromachining (WEMM) method, and the impact of vibration shape and vibration frequency on the machining quality is explored. A piezoelectric driven flexible mechanism is applied to generate elliptical trajectory on the cathode, the average value and root mean square error of the slit width are used to assess the machining quality. According to the experimental results, the elliptic vibration assisted WEMM reduce the machining width more effective than the one-dimensional vibration, but the root mean square error of the slit width is affected greatly by the vibration shape and frequency. Based on the experimental results, the vibration parameters are optimized as vibration frequency 10 Hz and phase difference 45° of controlling signals.

articleTitle: Molecular Design of Thermophilic Esterase for the Highly Regioselective Acylation of Quercetin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The regioselective behaviour of the Thermophilic Esterase from the archaeon Archaeoglobus fulgidus (AFEST) towards quercetin, in the acetylation reaction was investigated through molecular modelling. A combined docking, molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics approach was used to study the positions, the orientations, the interactions of quercetin in the active site of AFEST and the accessibility of their hydroxyl groups to the catalytic residues. As a result, the thermophilic esterase mutant (AF-S48I) has been performed and provide a molecular-level explanation for the observed regioselectivity of AF-S48I towards the 4-OH groups of quercetin. These findings are in accordance with experimental data and give a suitable explanation, at an atomic level, of the regioselectivity of AFEST in quercetin acetylation.

articleTitle: Research on Glycated Hemoglobin Detection Method Based on Nanotechnology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Glycated hemoglobin is an important indicator for diagnosing diabetes and monitoring blood sugar control levels. This study establishes an analytical method for detecting glycated hemoglobin based on the immune enhancement technology of physically adsorbed nanospheres. The optimal reaction conditions were screened out: nanosphere particle size of 125 nm, nanosphere concentration of 2%, antibody concentration of 80 mg/L, buffer system of HEPES with a pH value of 7.5, Tween-20 concentration of 0.12%, sodium chloride concentration of 40 g/L, and glycerol concentration of 7%. Compared with high-performance liquid chromatography and immunochromatography, the evaluation indicators are as follows: analytical sensitivity of 0.08%, intra-batch CVs of 1.19%, 0.85% and 0.66% for detection concentrations of 3.18%, 6.36% and 11.13%, respectively, inter-batch CVs of 1.99%, 1.15% and 0.84%, respectively, a linear range of2.0%-16%, r: 0.9994, and a relative deviation within ±3.5% for external quality assessment. The established method for measuring glycated hemoglobin using nanosphere immune enhancement technology has high consistency with high-performance liquid chromatography in terms of precision and linear range, and is superior to immunochromatography. This method is suitable for fully automatic biochemical analyzers, with advantages such as high automation, fast detection speed, and low cost, which can meet the requirements of clinical testing.

articleTitle: Design of a Stick-Slip Actuated Microgripper with a Large Motion Stroke
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To obtain a millimeter scale operation stroke, this paper proposes a stick-slip actuated microgripper. The structure design process of the microgripper is presented where a T-shaped compliant mechanism composed of four leaftype compliant hinges is developed. In order to achieve large load capacity and stepping actuating, longitudinal-shear piezoelectric (PZT) actuator is adopted, where the longitudinal motion is used to adjust the friction between the driving foot and the sliding part, while the shear PZT actuator is employed to actuate the two jaws open and close. Then, the actuating principle of the longitudinal-shear PZT actuator and the stickslip actuated microgripper is illustrated, which demonstrates how the microgripper achieve millimeter motion strokes. Finally, simulation analysis is carried out to investigate the performance of the developed microgripper. It can be seen from the results of static analysis that the maximum deformation of the weak stiffness object is 9.39 μm when a grasping force with the amplitude of 1 N is applied.

articleTitle: Study on the Mechanical Properties of Ginsenoside Rg3 in Protecting Cardiomyocytes from Oxidative Damage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study aims to investigate how ginsenoside Rg3 (Rg3) can protect neonatal rat cardiomyocytes from damage caused by H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and how it affects the mechanical properties of the cells. The oxidative damage model of neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMS) was established using varying doses of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The viability of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-injured and Rg3-treated NRCMS was assessed using the MTT method to determine an effective intervention concentration of Rg3. Herein, atomic force microscopy (AFM) was employed to measure the height, Young's modulus, and adhesion of NRCMS. The results indicated that the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> led to oxidative damage of NRCMS showing reduced cell viability and mechanical changes. Furthermore, the Rg3 treatment showed a protective effect on H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-induced myocardial oxidative damage in suckling rats, which was proved to be closely related to the changes in cell mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Study of Detection Liquid for Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging of Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Atomic force microscope (AFM) is flexible to perform experiments in air, vacuum and liquid environments. It allows three-dimensional imaging of samples to obtain their physical properties with atomic spatial resolution and millisecond time resolution. Imaging in liquid environments is extremely important for biological samples. Due to the complexity of the liquid environment, its influence on imaging quality should not be ignored. In this work, an AFM detection liquid containing less ions and organic compounds was introduced. Mouse brain microvascular endothelial (bEnd.3) cells and the silicon wafer with dot matrix structures were imaged in different liquid environments via AFM in the QI mode. Then the quality of each image was evaluated by the gray-level variance product (SMD2) function. The detection liquid is conducive to improve the AFM imaging quality, especially for biological samples.

articleTitle: Anisotropic and Temperature-Dependent Mechanical Properties of TPDH-Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: TPDH-graphene is a newly predicted two-dimensional carbon material with exceptional physical properties, positioning it as a promising candidate for nanoelectronics applications. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigated the anisotropic properties of the material and assessed how temperature influences its mechanical behavior. The results demonstrate that TPDH-graphene shows significant mechanical anisotropy, displaying superior tensile toughness and fracture strength along the zigzag direction in comparison to the armchair direction. At high temperatures up to 1200 K, the material exhibits a certain degree of tensile toughness in the armchair direction.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Analytical Properties of Anti-Cyclic Citrulline Peptide Antibody Reagents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Based on the principle of nanoparticle immuno turbidimetry, this study optimized the nanoparticle particle size, buffer pH, activator concentration and sealer concentration in the anti-cyclic citrulline peptide antibody detection system. The precision, linear interval and accuracy of the optimized reagent were evaluated on Hitachi 7170, Beckman AU480 and Mindray BS2000 automatic biochemical analyzers. The optimal detection system was obtained through optimization, and the detection linear interval was 3.5 U/ml-1000 U/mL, which was better than the linear range of domestic kits, solved the problem of false negative samples, and effectively avoided the appearance of hook effect. At the same time, its precision and accuracy can also meet the needs of clinical use.

articleTitle: Surface Quality Analysis of Laser-Induced Assisted Grinding of Single-Crystal Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The semiconductor material single-crystal silicon is known for its mechanical and chemical stability, which poses several challenges for micro-machining. These challenges include difficulty in material removal, potential surface damage, and limited machining precision, among others. Therefore, this paper proposes using laser-induced assisted grinding (L-IAG) technology to modify the surface of single-crystal silicon. By combining this technique with an abrasive grinding process, the integrity of the grinding surface can be improved. In L-IAG, laser irradiation is applied to the surface of single-crystal silicon. This irradiation generates the oxide layer with a looser density compared to the original silicon material. The looser oxide film is then removed in the subsequent grinding process. This method reduces the surface damage to the workpiece, improves the surface quality, and decreases the surface roughness. In this study, the surface morphology and surface roughness of conventional grinding (CG) and L-IAG were compared through experimental analysis. The results showed that L-IAG effectively improves the surface finish quality of single-crystal silicon. With CG, the surface roughness of the workpiece was 1.150 μm. In contrast, using L-IAG reduced the surface roughness to 0.587 μm, representing a 49% improvement.

articleTitle: Design of Bionic Deployable Wing Based on the Hindwing of Asian Ladybird
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: About the developing of Flapping-Wing Micro Robots (FWMRs), the intricate deployable hindwings of beetles present a practical template for innovation. In this paper, the Asian ladybird is selected as the bio-inspired object. The movement of the Asian ladybird during its take-off and landing is captured by high-speed camera to obtain the folding and unfolding mode of its hindwings. Building on these observations, a novel bio-inspired deployable wing configuration for FWMRs is conceptualized. The proposed design undergoes a rigorous evaluation of its mechanical motions and aerodynamic attributes through simulation. This study aims to provide a substantive technical foundation for the design of FWMRs deployable wings.

articleTitle: Addressing Mechanical and Electrochemical Aging of Cylindrical LFP Battery Cells by Laser Structuring of Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: First results for the implementation of ultrafast laser structured thick-film lithium iron phosphate (LFP) electrodes in cylindrical battery cells are presented, with a special focus on laser structuring without thermal modification of the active material and the winding quality of thick-film electrodes. It was shown in half-cell measurements that minor thermal modifications did not result in a reduction in specific capacity of laser structured electrodes. Cells with structured electrodes had a higher rate capability at discharge C-rates greater than 1C compared to cells with unstructured electrodes. Furthermore, line structured electrodes with a structure pitch of 300 μm showed no visible damage of the electrode coating after winding at a radius of 3 mm, whereby the unstructured reference electrodes showed visible crack formation and delamination from the current collector after winding at a radius of 5 mm.

articleTitle: Thread Features Surface Morphology of C/SiC Composites by Laser-Ultrasonic Hybrid Machining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced silicon carbide (C/SiC) composites belong to the category of ceramic matrix composites, presenting the anisotropy and inhomogeneity of the material, and is a highly hard and brittle material, resulting in the machining of the thread characteristics of the tooth tip is missing, the poor quality of the surface and other problems. The quality of ceramic matrix composites is significantly improved through the use of laser-ultrasonic hybrid machining (L-UHM) which has been a hot topic in recent years. Focusing on the impact of L-UHM on the surface morphology of C/SiC composite thread features after machining with different parameters. The impact of process methods on the surface topography of C/SiC composite threaded features after machining were investigated by conducting conventional machining (CM), laser-assisted machining (LAM), and L-UHM tests. The results showed that in both the parallel and vertical fiber directions of the tooth top, the matrix breakage was significantly reduced which improved structural integrity compared with CM and LAM.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Proximity Effect Correction in Electron Beam Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The proximity effect caused by electron scattering leads to pattern deviation in electron beam lithography. Traditional two-dimensional proximity effect correction methods is ineffective for fine and three-dimensional structures, particularly at the edges and corners of the patterns. A novel 'A+V' type three-dimensional proximity effect correction method based on dose correction is proposed in this paper. The Monte Carlo method and cell removal development technique are used to simulate the three-dimensional energy density distribution and development process, respectively. Deconvolution of the three-dimensional energy density distribution provides the dose distribution at the pattern edges, and distribution of development rate is used to determine the dose distribution of the other areas in the pattern. The study also investigates the effect of dose distribution on the three-dimensional morphology of the resist. Case study is examined on a L-shaped pattern. Simulation results indicate that compared to uncorrected and two-dimensional proximity effect correction methods, the three-dimensional proximity effect correction approach proposed in this paper shows significant improvements in the accuracy and precision of electron beam lithography.

articleTitle: A Space-Type 4-DOF Precision Operation Stage with A Large Stroke Three-Stage Motion Amplification Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This research presents a large stroke three-stage motion amplification mechanism (MAM) space-type 4-DOF precision operation stage. In response to the size limitation of piezoelectric actuators (PEAs), a novel three-stage MAM is developed to provide a vast workspace. The three-stage MAM is folded to create a compact structure, drawing inspiration from the deployable construction. The pseudo rigid body model (PRBM) technique was used to model the kinematics of the XY table, and the workspace and kinematic performance of the XY and Z stages were analyzed by finite element analysis. The findings of the simulation indicate that the X- and Y- axis can move up to 254.5 μm in maximum output. The motion amplification ratios can reach 25.4 in the X- and Y- axis. The output displacement and output angle can reach 10.1 μm and 0.33 rad in the Z-axis. The first natural frequency of the XY platform and the Z platform are up to 143.5 Hz and 1748 Hz. The precision operation stage designed in this paper provides greater operational flexibility for the operating tool.

articleTitle: A Study on the Imobilization Method of E. coli for AFM Detection under Physiological Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The micro-nano manipulation techniques based on Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is an important tool for studying the morphology and mechanical properties of bacteria under physiological conditions. However, immobilizing the bacteria on the substrate is the key obstacle for AFM detection in liquid condition. In this study, the methods of embedding and adsorption were combined to improve the immobilization efficiency. Compared to E. coli on a non-structured base surface, E. coli on a structured base surface appears more stretched out and is less likely to aggregate. It grown along the structure of the substrate, achieving nanomanipulation to a certain extent. This study will provide a new immobilization method for microorganism as well as E. coli.

articleTitle: Effect of Rejuvenation on Properties of Amorphous-Crystalline TiNiCu Alloy Ribbons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Layered amorphous-crystalline ribbons of rapidly quenched TiNiCu alloy with two-way shape memory effect (TWSME) have proven to be a promising material for microtweezers used for the gripping and manipulation of micro- and nanoscale objects. Ribbons with different crystalline layer thicknesses have been produced in this work by melt spinning at variable melt cooling rate. A method has been proposed and an innovative experimental setup has been designed for TWSME studies. We show that reducing the melt cooling rate one can increase the thickness of the crystalline layer, accompanied by an increase in the minimum ribbon bending radius and the maximum reversible deformation during the implementation of the TWSME. The test ribbon samples have been rejuvenation treated (cryogenic thermocycling). It has been shown that cryothermal treatment can tangibly increase the TWSME reversible deformation and significantly reduce the width of the shape change temperature hysteresis. The latter effect can be used for improving the performance of microdevices, in particular microtweezers, based on rapidly quenched amorphous-crystalline ribbons.

articleTitle: Development of an Electronic Target-Type Optical Performance Calibration Device for Medical Rigid Endoscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: An electronic target-type medical rigid endoscope optical performance calibration device is proposed. The device consists of a special electronic target display screen, a special high-definition camera lens, a video image acquisition system, a digital image processing computer, a multi-dimensional adjustment table, an angle encoder and a software module. It can analyze a number of optical parameters such as the field of view angle of the pupil of medical rigid endoscopes, the angle of view direction, the relative distortion of the unit and the optical efficiency of the imaging mirror body at the calibration customer's site.

articleTitle: Visual Focusing and Levelling Precision System Towards Mini/MicroLED Panel Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In order to improve the focus quality and efficiency of Mini/MicroLED chip panel defect detection, we focus our research on visual focusing and levelling techniques. This paper reports on the construction of Image focus evaluation method based on Gaussian fuzzy difference (F-GFD), and the method of focus adjustment and leveling based on ZTTθ leveling and correcting motion stage is also proposed. By optimising and adjusting the parameters, the image focus evaluation method (F-GFD) has a high focus resolution and high sensitivity effect, which has an axial resolution better than 1.25 μm axial resolution. Experiments show that the image focus evaluation method (F-GFD) combined with ZTTθ stage can realize multi-points focus of Mini/MicroLED panel and the leveling process of panel and image plane, which further provides a basis for solving the defocus problem caused by panel warping in the defect detection of Mini/MicroLED chips.

articleTitle: Molecular Mechanisms Of Beta-Amyloid Blockage Under The Action Of Natural Compounds And Its Nanoformulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Amyloidosis represents serious disease caused by the amyloid protein deposition in many tissues and organs, including heart, brain, vessels, nerves, etc. Protein deposition drastically changes the functionality of the organs and systems, leading in its abnormal functions and even death. To inhibit or decelerate the deposition several natural small molecules can be used. In this paper such natural small molecules and its molecular mechanisms are considered. The developed drug delivery systems for tafamidis and diflunisal based on biosafe as well as biodegradable polymer matrix such as hyaluronic acid are also presented.

articleTitle: Design and Analyses of a Heavy-Load and Large-Stroke Micro-Positioning Tip-Tilt Stage with Flexure Levitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The tip-tilt micro-positioning stage designed for laser-induced massive transfer of microLED needs to withstand external loads up to 20 kg and provide motion range up to millimeter-scale. This paper introduces a flexure-levitated large-stroke, heavy-load tip-tilt micro-positioning stage specifically designed for microLED laser-based massive transfer. It employs a compliant constant-force mechanism to design flexure levitation units that provide nearly constant support to the moving platform within the millimeter-scale travel range, achieving a quasi-levitated effect. Utilizing finite element analysis, the paper conducts parameter analysis to design a compliant constant-force mechanism based on positive and negative stiffness combinations. A analytical model of the flexure-levitated micro-stage is established to analyze its stiffness characteristics and constant-force properties. The system’s equivalent stiffness of the flexure-levitated tip-tilt micro-positioning significantly decreases, resulting in reduced driving forces and simplified force control methods. However, this approach also lowers the inherent natural frequency, necessitating the implementation of flexible supports for adjustment of dynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: Insights into Droplet Impact Dynamics on Microstructured Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This research examines the effects of water droplet impact on superhydrophobic surfaces made from laser-fabricated Inconel 718 alloy. The interaction between water droplets and microstructured surfaces at both micro and macro levels was investigated using a phase-field model, aiming to simulate and elucidate intricate mechanisms involved. The superhydrophobic surfaces were fabricated using a synergistic approach that combines laser micro-texturing and chemical modification, resulting in water contact angles exceeding 150° and exceptionally low rolling angles. The meticulously designed micropillar arrays on the Inconel 718 substrates were found to play a pivotal role in the impact dynamics, significantly influencing the rebound behavior and stability of the impinging water droplets. Furthermore, this study reveals that surfaces with different contact angles lead to distinct final states of the water droplets post-impact. This research not only deepens our fundamental understanding of the dynamic behavior of water droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces but also provides theoretical guidance and experimental basis for designing and optimizing superhydrophobic surfaces, which holds immense importance for the applications in relevant industries.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Monolithic Tilt/Tip Platform Based on Anti-Symmetric Flexible Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the development of precision machinery, there is a growing demand for space-based mechanical mechanisms with micro/nano precision such as tilt/tip stages. Here, we propose a design of a tilt/tip stage capable of biaxial deflection based on additive manufacturing, offering the high spatial compactness of the overall structure. The two axial offsets are driven by two piezoelectric ceramics (PZT), which are fixed on a set of orthogonally biased bridge amplifiers with dual symmetry in structure and drive. The horizontal displacement of the sideboard drives the two connected elliptical beams with different stiffnesses to deform in opposite directions, resulting in a biased pendulum motion of the actuating plane. This design features a compact overall size, high first-order module and stable operation. Individual deflection of x-axis and y-axis, as well as multi-angle deflection between them, can be achieved with minimal parasitic displacement. Results shows that the tilt/tip stage has a first order mode state of 968.17 Hz. The maximum biaxial deflection angle is 6.73 mrad when inputting 20 μm displacement. This work offers a novel concept for the future biaxial tilt/tip stage designs.

articleTitle: Effect of Laser Sintering Parameters on Semiconductor Nanoparticle Coarsening
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Selective laser sintering (SLS) of micro- and nanoparticles has become a key additive manufacturing technology for engineered components and conformal circuits, and the laser sintering properties of various polymers, metals, and ceramic powders have been widely researched. However, unlike the intuitive grain coarsening and density enhancement of metal and ceramic powders during sintering, semiconductor nanomaterials are accompanied by physicochemical processes including grain coarsening, substance diffusion, and elemental precipitation under photovoltaic and photothermal interactions, which complicate the modulation of their electrical and thermoelectric properties. Here we investigate the effects of laser power, scanning speed, hatch distance, preheating temperature and scanning duty cycle on the laser sintering temperature of ITO and In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles. The results show that laser power, scanning speed and hatch distance are handles for fine-tuning of sintering temperature, while preheating temperature and scanning duty cycle allow for a wide range of sintering temperature tuning. In addition, the sintered/molten microscopic morphology and electrical properties of semiconductor nanoparticles at different sintering temperatures are further analyzed, which offer parameter optimization and performance enhancement references for lasering of semiconductor nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Au-MPN@Ag Nanocomposite-Assisted Mass Spectrometry for Metabolite Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Sensitive detection of metabolites in biofluids plays an important role in disease diagnosis. Herein, we synthesized a novel noble metal based nanocomposite using metal-polyphenol network (MPN) as coordination and redox reaction. The formed Au-MPN@Ag nanocomposite exhibited excellent metabolite detection performance in laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS). Notably, Au-MPN@Ag nanocomposite based LDI-MS platform achieved direct detection of metabolites in biofluids without any sample pretreatment. Our work provides a new advanced platform for metabolic analysis towards in vitro diagnostics.

articleTitle: Liquid-Phase vs CVD Routes to 2D Polymeric Phthalocyanines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: We discuss synthetic routes to 2D polymeric phthalocyanines. Among them, CVD (chemical vapor deposition) is the most efficient technique to obtain highly-ordered polymers. The major disadvantage of CVD route is that bulk polymer can not be obtained in this way. We propose a new technique that is based on a chemical reaction performed in a boiling paraffin. We report detailed study of physical properties of FePPC, including structure, Mössbauer spectra, magnetic properties and conductivity. These data would be impossible to obtain for a CVD-synthesized thin film.

articleTitle: Study on the Detection of Pancreatic Cancer Tumor Markers Based on Planar DNA Nanostructure Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Pancreatic cancer is a malignant tumor of the digestive system with a high mortality rate. MiRNA21 is a common tumor marker for the detection of pancreatic cancer. In this study, DNA nanostructures were used as biological recognition elements, and electrochemical detection methods were used to design biosensors for known pancreatic cancer marker miRNAs. The sensor is evaluated on the basis of theoretical design structure. The detection limit was 1fM-1uM, the fitting curve was y = –1.4886 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–6</sup> log (x) + 1.1761 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–4</sup>, and the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value was 0.9573. A modular biosensor with strong specificity, high sensitivity and simple operation was established for the detection of miRNA, which was of great significance for the early diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. It can save manpower, material resources and time, and is an important supplement to traditional molecular biology research methods and clinical detection methods.

articleTitle: Scanning Joule Expansion Microscopy Based on Lateral Deflection for Improved Nanoscale Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The shrinking scale of microelectronics necessitates temperature measurement at the nanometer level. Here, we report a new work mode of Scanning Joule Expansion Microscopy (SJEM) technique which pioneering utilizes lateral deflection signals to demodulate thermal expansion on sample surfaces. Compared with traditional SJEM, this mode provides an adjustable sensitivity by changing the contact (frictional) force. As a result, the detection limit of this mode is improved by more than an order of magnitude. Additionally, in-plane and out-of-plane expansions can be distinguished through trace and retrace lines, providing a comprehensive analysis of thermal behaviors.

articleTitle: Metal Ion-Tannic Acid Network-Coated Gold Nanoparticles for Metabolite Analysis by Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study introduced metal ion-tannic acid network-coated gold nanoparticles (M-TA@AuNPs) as novel matrices for laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI MS). M-TA@AuNPs as matrices could enhance the LDI MS performance for detection of metabolites at low molecular weight with low background noise, which overcame the limitations of organic matrices and bare AuNPs. Subsequently, the proposed method was applied in the analysis of complex biological samples including urine and cerebrospinal fluid, with high signal intensity (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>). Our work demonstrated the good potential of M-TA@AuNPs as LDI MS matrices in metabolic profiling and clinical diagnostics.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes
Index Terms: High-angle Annular Dark-field Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy

articleTitle: Fundamental Nanostructures Obtained by Hydrogel Photoresist in Laser Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Photoresist materials have been developed in many varieties to improve their stability and sensitivity during the lithography process. Compared with other photoresist materials, HEMA-co-MMA is a material with superior performance. In this paper, hydrogel nanostructures are obtained by material of HEMA-co-MMA and laser interference lithography. The spin-coating speeds, exposure to different laser powers and different exposure times have been investigated. According to the observation of the microstructure of the formed grating patterns, that the desired grating structures on the photolithography pattern is achieved by spin-coating speed of 4,000 rpm, spin-coating thickness of 2 μm, exposure dose of 120 mJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-190 mJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, laser power of 500 mW, and exposure time of 3 s. This implies that the copolymer HEMA-co-MMA is suitable for photolithography of nanostructures.

articleTitle: Investigation of Lateral Force in Tip-Based Nanofabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Tip based nanofabrication has a wide application in micro/nano devices. Scratching depth is a key indicator of the machining quality. Tip tilt occurs during scratching process due to the low rigidity. Current depth models usually ignore the tip tilt. To study the effect of tip tilt on scratching depth, a series of scratching experiment is conducted to collect deformation signals of the cantilever. The tip tilt signal is used to rectify the actual scratching length. The rigidity of cantilever is obtained based on simulation and calibration experiments. Lateral force and normal force are calculated using the calibrated rigidity. Based on the measured force and rectified scratching length, an empirical model of lateral force is established in the edge forward and face forward direction. The apparent friction coefficient is also fitted in these two directions and a simplified analytical model is proposed to analyze the variation of apparent friction coefficient.

articleTitle: Silicon Based Integrated Plasmonic Schottky Spectral-polarization Detector Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The spectral and polarization characteristics of objects are crucial in astronomy, remote sensing, and medical applications. Conventional photodetectors require multiple measurements to capture spectral and polarization information. However, existing spectral-polarization detectors face challenges such as poor real-time performance and integration difficulties. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative silicon-based plasmonic Schottky spectral-polarization detector array. Multiple plasmonic Schottky detectors on a single chip enables simultaneous detection of spectral characteristics and linear polarization properties. In this experiment, the detector array exhibited peak absorption in the range of wavelength from 450 to 900 nm and demonstrated fine linear dichroism (LD) at their absorption peak wavelengths. This shows its capability to simultaneously acquire spectral and linear polarization information in applications such as material analysis, scatter imaging, and medical diagnostics. Additionally, due to its high compatibility with CMOS processes, the device can potentially be monolithically integrated with CMOS circuits. By optimizing its performance in the future, we can develop on-chip spectral-polarization detectors capable of detecting full polarization states across a wide range of wavelengths.

articleTitle: A Convolution Neural Network Based Algorithm for More Accurate Spectrum Reconstruction of Miniaturized Spectrometers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To address the optimization challenges related to device count and responsivities in miniaturized spectrometers, we introduce an optimized strategy based on convolution neural networks (CNNs). This approach employs nonlinear techniques to mitigate issues arising from excessive similarity within the response matrix. Concurrently, we incorporate a matrix similarity computation method, superseding the conventional approach of resolving underdetermined equation sets, which enhances the precision of spectral reconstruction. The experiments demonstrate that under identical conditions, our method achieves an average central wavelength deviation of 1.2 nm for spectra with a single peak, which is lower than that of compressed sensing (CS) at 1.9 nm and CNN at 2.1 nm. The mean squared error (MSE) for reconstructing spectra with double peaks is 4.89e-3, representing an order of magnitude reduction compared to other algorithms, exhibiting unique advantages in both image quality and parameters.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on the Fabrication of Microscale Metal Patterns via Femtosecond Laser-Induced Electrodeposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Femtosecond laser-induced electrodeposition (FLIED) process is a maskless additive manufacturing technique that facilitates the precise fabrication of micro-scale copper patterns. The process parameters, namely applied voltage (U) and scanning speed (v), were systematically varied in the current FLIED study to investigate their impacts on layer height and width. The analytical data obtained from 9 sets of parametric experiments were utilized to develop a binary linear regression equation through the application of multiple linear regression analysis, specifically focusing on the relationship between layer height and layer width. The objective of this study was to establish a quantitative correlation between the process parameters U and v, and the dimensions of layer height and width. For all experiments, 10 mm diameter stainless steel substrates were utilized and the optimum solution thickness for FLIED was determined.

articleTitle: Real-Time Fluorescent Quantitative PCR for Detection of Peripheral Blood T-Cell Lymphoma
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) is a group of rare and highly heterogeneous malignant diseases of the lymphatic system derived from mature, post-thymic T cells. In this work, a qPCR assay was constructed for RHOA G17V and IDH2 R172 mutations by extracting genomic DNA from PTCL cells. The performance validation shown that mutant reaction solution specific detected RHOA G17V and IDH2 R172 mutations, the limit of detection (LOD) was 1% mutation ratio, the accuracy RSD were less than 2.5%, and the repeatability RSD were less than 2%. The work provide a realtime fluorescent quantitative PCR for detection of peripheral blood T-cell lymphoma, it is a laboratory guidance and reference for the development of PTCL qPCR diagnostic kits.

articleTitle: Megasonic Power Supply Design for Precision Cleaning of Nanoimprint Stencils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In the process of nanoimprint lithography, the surface of the template is easily contaminated by various particles, such as dust and photoresist, which directly affect the accuracy and quality of the lithography process. Therefore, the cleaning of the template is particularly crucial. This paper designs a megasonic power supply for the precision cleaning of lithography molds, given the significant advantages of megasonic cleaning technology in this application. The system comprises seven main modules: main control, adjustable DC power supply, drive, power, High-frequency transformers, impedance matching, and voltage and current acquisition. The power conversion and control scheme employs an adjustable DC power module and a half-bridge inverter circuit, enabling stable and accurate control of output power at ultra-high megahertz frequencies. Additionally, the power supply utilizes a two-stage LC impedance matching network with high bandwidth and frequency tracking, ensuring efficient and uniform output of megahertz-level drive electrical signals. Verification has shown that the megasonic power supply can continuously and stably output 400W and 1-3MHz electrical signals to drive the operation of the megasonic transducer.

articleTitle: Bacterial 1anomotion: Detection with Atomic Force Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Useful instrument for biology and medicine on the nanolevel is atomic force microscope. It can be used for study of nanomotion because in addition to usual movements (by flagella), bacteria also have a special type of movement – motion in the nanoscale diapason. This property can be detected with high sensitive methods only, like oscillation mode of atomic force microscopy. During nanomotion can be detected amplitude and frequency. The amplitude and frequency of nanomotion can be used for detection of bacterial antibiotic resistance and species of microorganism.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Micro-Nano Grooved Structures with Biocompatibility by Laser Interference Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this study, a laser interference lithography step splicing system was set up to fabricate the U-groove structures in microscale on the surface of titanium alloy and the differences in surface morphology, surface roughness, and water friendly and hydrophobic were analyzed to study the effect on cell behaviors. The micro U-groove structures with period of 10um caused both increased surface roughness and the contact angle of water. The MG63 cells were cultured on micro U-groove structures and cell proliferation, adhesion and spreading were analyzed after 24,48 and 72 hours by MTT and different assays. The results showed that the well-desgined micro U-groove structures had a significant positive effects on the proliferation of the MG63 cells, The width ratio of 8:2 of the U-groove structures was beneficial to promote the spread and growth of the MG63 cells.

articleTitle: Optimization Design and Performance Research on Two-Stage Reduction Micro-Drive Mechanism Based on Particle Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: High precision positioning operation in small space is of great significance in aerospace, biomedicine, precision instruments, and other fields. In order to obtain smaller displacement and higher accuracy, this paper focuses on the structural optimization, design and performance analysis of the two-stage reduction micro-drive mechanism. In order to obtain the maximum reduction ratio, the particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) was used to optimize the structure of the mechanism. The finite element method was used to analyze the dynamic and kinematic properties of the optimized two-stage reduced structure system. The analysis results show that the reduction micro-drive mechanism does not resonate with the piezoelectric ceramic during operation, and the dynamic performance of the mechanism meets the design requirements. The analysis results show that the mechanism can achieve a reduction ratio of 24.73:1 from the piezoelectric ceramic as the input displacement to the output displacement of the design mechanism, and it meets the design requirements in terms of motion performance. From the above, it can be seen that the mechanism has good dynamic performance, large reduction ratio and high motion accuracy. This paper is of great significance for the research in the fields of advanced precision mechanical motion and micro-drive mechanism.

articleTitle: Advanced Upconversion Nanoparticles for Improved Endothelial Barrier Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) have been used in bio-imaging because they can emit light under the excitation with longer wavelength. However, the poor transportation of UCNPs crossing tissue barriers results in inefficient delivery of UCNPs to the targeted organ/tissues. Herein, the core-shell UCNPs modified with cationic biopolymer, i.e., N, N-trimethyl chitosan (TMC), have been developed for improved endothelial barrier transport. The core-shell UCNPs with the average particle size of 26.05±3.72 nm have the emission at 443 nm under the excitation of 908 nm. The core-shell UCNPs have been further modified with biocompatible polymers to enhance water dispersibility, and surface charge positivity. In addition, the transport ability of the core-shell UCNPs has been investigated by using an in vitro endothelial barrier model.
