The results indicate that TMC modified on the surface of core-shell UCNPs can significantly improve the endothelial barrier transport by two times as compared to core-shell UCNPs without TMC.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Ultra-Thick Cathode for Superior-Performance Lithium Metal Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The thick electrodes of lithium metal batteries (LMB) will increase their capacity and energy density, but their high internal resistance leads to low power density and poor rate performance. However, due to the increase in internal resistance, there are limitations in simultaneously improving energy density and power density. This article uses femtosecond laser to process lithium iron phosphate cathode. In micrometer scale groove structures, increasing the contact region between the electrolyte and electrode helps to improve the electrochemical reaction rate and ion transfer rate of the electrode. Compared with the original electrode, under the condition of 2 C, the rate performance of the structured thick electrode has been improved by three times, the surface discharge capacity has been increased by two times, and it can stably cycle more than 1800 times at 750 mA/g, with a Coulombic efficiency close to 100%.

articleTitle: Performance Validation Study of Allergen-Specific IgE Quantum Dot Test Kits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study conducted a performance validation of allergen-specific IgE quantum dot test kits. The variability (CV%) in precision testing ranged from 7.72% (Codfish) to 12.39% (Soybean). The recovery rates in accuracy testing were all between 85% and 115%. The proportion of samples with blank limit validation less than or equal to 0.1 IU/mL was 100%, with a minimum of 87%. The proportion of samples with detection limit validation greater than or equal to 0.2 IU/mL was 100%, with a minimum of 87%. The proportion of samples with quantitative limit validation deviation (TE) ≤15% was 100%, with a minimum of 88%.

articleTitle: Research on Laser Repair Technology for Micro-LED Display Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To enhance the manufacturing quality of Micro-LED display panels, in-situ removal and replacement repair of defective Micro-LED chips are essential. Experimental ablation of Micro-LED chips using single-point lasers analyzed erosion characteristics under different laser spot overlap rates. Optimization of process parameters achieved rapid and precise removal and high-quality leveling of solder pad surfaces. Single-point laser soldering experiments on Micro-LED chips analyzed bonding characteristics under varying temperatures, and times, achieving high-quality re-bonding and high-brightness light emission. providing important guidance for the rapid repair of defective chips in the large-scale production of medium and large Micro-LED displays.

articleTitle: Design of a Bio-Inspired Magnetic Soft Microrobot for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Magnetic soft microrobots, with their wireless control and inherent safety, hold great potential in the biomedical field. However, achieving effective mobility in complex environments such as the gastrointestinal tract remains a challenge. Inspired by the golden wheel spider, which utilizes a rolling motion to navigate rapidly through desert terrain, this paper proposes a soft microrobot capable of overcoming obstacles through a similar rolling motion driven by an external rotating magnetic field. The soft microrobot is composed of a silicone body and four micro-magnets for propulsion. Experimental results demonstrate that the magnetic soft microrobot exhibits excellent mobility in irregular anatomical cavities, navigating three-dimensional pathways with vertical distances up to 8 cm. These results highlight the significant potential of the soft microrobot for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis on Cutting AISI 1045 with Micro-Textured Tools Based on ABAQUS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: AISI 1045 steel is extensively used in mechanical manufacturing, aerospace, and the automotive industry due to its exceptional mechanical properties. However, its high strength, hardness, and wear resistance will lead to rapid tool wear during cutting, thereby reducing tool life and affecting machining efficiency. The application of micro-textures on the tool surface has demonstrated the potential to reduce tool wear and extend tool life in dry cutting conditions, thereby promoting green machining practices. Optimizing textured parameters is essential for enhancing tool cutting performance. This study explores the impact of different micro-textured parameters on cutting performance of the AISI 1045 steel by designing three sets of micro-pit textured tools with different spacings. Finite element simulations were conducted to evaluate the cutting performance, with a particular focus on variations in shear angle, cutting force, and cutting temperature. The results indicate that micro-pit textured tools significantly improve cutting performance by the increase in shear angle, the reduction in cutting force, and mitigating high-temperature buildup on the tool surface. Among the different spacings, the 80 pm spaced micro-pit textured tool exhibited the best performance in terms of enhancing shear angle, cutting force, and reducing cutting temperature, followed by tools with 100 μm and 200 μm spacings.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Cytoplasmic Solubility of Heparinase I from Flavobacterium Heparinum in Escherichia Coli by Adding a Polycationic Peptide Tag and Co-Expression with CpkA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Objective: Heparinase is essential for heparin production and application. HepA derivedfrom Flavobacterium heparinum, is the most widely studied heparinase I. Recombinant HepA is difficult to express as its soluble form in Escherichia coli. For this reason, many studies have attempted to grow the addition of different kinds of labels at the N-terminus can help increase the solubility of HepA in the cytoplasm. In this study, we engineered a polycationic six-peptide tag, called an "anchor tag" (GGRRGR),with increased affinity for the chaperonin CpkA from Thermococcus kodakarensis, in an attempt to increase the cytoplasmic solubility of HepA. Firstly, HepA was fused with GGRRGR at its N-terminus and then subcloned in the plasmid pET21a, resulting in pET21a-HepA'. The modified HepA (HepA') was then expressed alongside pACYCDuet-1-CpkA. The results revealed that the amount of insoluble HepA' was reduced while the amount of soluble HepA' increased to 95% of the total soluble fraction of E. coli lysate. Furthermore, the specific activity of HepA' in the crude enzyme extract was 48.5 IU/mg, suggesting that the crude HepA' was almost ready for catalyzing. The specific activity of HepA' after purification (~146 IU/mg) was comparable to that of native HepA (~130 IU/mg), indicating that the polycationic peptide tag does not interfere with heparinase activity. In summary, our results showed that the co-expression of polycationic peptide tag-fused HepA with CpkA resulted in an active and soluble form of heparinase.

articleTitle: Design of Electromagnetic Force Loading Device for Ultrasonic Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Ultrasonic transducers are widely used in micro-nano operations, precision manufacturing and other fields, and their working performance is closely related to changes in working load. This paper combines the equivalent magnetic circuit method and finite element analysis (FEA), based on the principle of electromagnetic force, to design a working load simulation loading device for high-frequency ultrasonic transducers, completed the design and optimization of the magnetic circuit structural parameters, and produced a device prototype. Upon conducting performance evaluations, it was observed that the simulated loading device demonstrated a force-to-flow ratio of 12.39 N/A, which laid a good foundation for research on the electrical and dynamic characteristics of the transducer, resonant frequency tracking and output amplitude control under different working loads.

articleTitle: Nonisochronicity of Ferromagnetic Thin Films with Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy Subjected to Bias Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The impact of bias magnetic field on the nonlinearity of ferromagnetic thin films is investigated. Using the methods of Hamiltonian formalism, an analytical expression for the nonisochronicity coefficient is obtained taking into account perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. We show that in films with high perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, an effective adjustment ofthe nonlinearity can be performed by a lower bias magnetic field. Theoretically obtained results are verified by micromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Development of a Duplex qPCR Assay for the Rapid Detection of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To build a duplex qPCR system that quickly and accurately detects the MTB. Specific primers and TaqMan probes were designed for the IS6110 and gyrB genes of MTB respectively, to optimize the qPCR system for the simultaneous detection of the two genes in a single tube, and the recombinant plasmids of the IS6110 and gyrB genes were used as the standards to establish a standard curve to validate the sensitivity, the specificity and reproducibility of the method. The duplex qPCR system for MTB was successfully constructed, and the slopes of the standard curves for IS6110 and gyrB were -3.521 and -3.572, the values of R2 value were 0.991 and 0.993 and the lowest limit of detection was 100 copies/mL. It was with high specificity. It has no amplification signals for non-tuberculous Mycobacteria and good reproducibility, and the coefficients of variation of the intra-assay precision and inter-assay precision was less than 1%. In this experiment, the establishment of the duplex qPCR system for MTB has good sensitivity, specificity and reproducibility, which is of great significance for the rapid and accurate detection of MTB.

articleTitle: Monolithic Fabrication and Surface Metalization of Single-Crystal Suspended Sub-Micron Si Nanowires with 3D MEMS Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Thanks to their superior mechanical, electrical, and optical characteristics, silicon nanowires attract much attention in applications ranging from biochemical sensors and inertial measurement devices to energy storage systems. This study introduces a new method for the scalable production and monolithic integration of sub-micron silicon nanowires with microelectromechanical systems. In-plane (width) and out-of-plane (thickness) critical dimensions of 600 nm and 300 nm, respectively, are demonstrated for sub-micron silicon nanowires with an etch depth of up to 50 μm. Finally, the use of stencil lithography is also demonstrated by selective coating of sub-micron silicon nanowires with a gold layer. Having moderately larger dimensions compared to silicon nanowires, their sub-micron counterparts proved to cut fabrication costs and relieve fabrication-related challenges, as they improve yield and repeatability while they impart added functionality to electromechanical sensors, whose further miniaturization heavily relies on such multiscale processes.

articleTitle: Biomechanics of Stem Cells: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Biomechanics of stem cells has garnered significant attention in the field of stem cell biology and regenerative medicine due to its role in regulating stem cell fate. However, the regulation of stem cell fate through biomechanics involves complex signal transduction mechanisms that rely on protein receptors, fibre networks, and signalling pathways to convert biomechanical signals in the stem cell microenvironment into biochemical signals. The development of AFM, microfluidic chip, and 3D cell culture technologies has provided the means to study stem cell biomechanics and its regulation of stem cell fate. Meanwhile, this paper highlights the challenges and future directions of stem cell biomechanics in guiding stem cell differentiation. It describes and analyses the transduction mechanism and technical means of stem cell biomechanics that regulate stem cell fate. This paper also provides discussions on biomechanically guided stem cell differentiation in the field of regenerative medicine.

articleTitle: Smart Nanopipette Technology for Studying 2D and 3D Cancer Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for studying 3D spheroids using glass nanopipettes and nanoelectrodes. The innovative application of these tools allows the investigation of spheroids from multiple perspectives. The first demonstration of this approach involved the use of scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM), which enabled the spheroidal surface topography of U87MG (human glioblastoma) to be obtained for the first time. This was complemented by the mapping of Young's module. Furthermore, the electrochemical approach enabled the internal oxygen, reactive oxygen species(ROS) profiles to be obtained within the spheroids formed from primary cortical neurons and U87MG spheroids, representing a novel advancement in this field. The principal advantage of nanocapillary-based electrodes is their ability to perform minimally invasive measurements in the interior regions of spheroids, thereby facilitating precise electrochemical detection of oxygen and ROS levels at a given spheroid depth. This technological advance represents a significant step forward, opening up new opportunities for minimally invasive, high-resolution spheroid studies that can improve the development of therapies for tumor and neurodegenerative diseases.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of a Kind of Compliant Constant Force Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Compliant constant force mechanism has the characteristic of outputting constant force. In this article, the optimization design method of a kind of parallel compliant constant force mechanism is studied. The approach utilizes finite element analysis in conjunction with a multi-objective genetic optimization algorithm (MOGA) as its foundation. It is segregated into two processes: Firstly, the theoretical analysis process of the constant force mechanism is introduced. The mechanism is composed of a double V beam and a bistable beam in parallel. The double V beam provides positive stiffness, and the bistable beam provides negative stiffness. After determining the constant force characteristics and initial design parameters, the multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) based on the finite element analysis results is used to optimize the model. It is verified by finite element simulation that the optimized model can have a large constant force stroke. The finite element simulation results show that compared with the initial structure, the constant force stroke of the optimized compliant constant force mechanism (CFM) is increased by 60%.

articleTitle: Phospholipid Bilayer Nanostructures Functionalized by Amide Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Using the contemporary structural methods Electromagnetic Echo Effect (EMEE) and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) we have studied structural and thermodynamical properties of model phospholipid bilayer nanocomposite-admixture 1-Stearoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (SOPC) / carbon nanotubes amide functionalized by [CON(CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>] group. The structural analysis developed allows the role of the SOPC bilayer structure distortion induced by amide functionalized nanotubes admixture to be identified. On the base of DSC analysis, a novel effect, laminar gel L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">β</inf> - liquid crystal L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> phase transition, driven by van’t Hoff enthalpy, pointing to an intermediate, partially cooperative phase transition and new intermediate state was discovered. We built a microscopical model of the fundamental laminar gel into liquid crystals phase transition including both bulk and surface forces, acting and balancing the bilayer structure conformation. Besides this and to explain the tenability of the bilayer structure conformation, including transmembrane process, by electro-optical (EO) excitation, we have modulated the evolution and the growth of the bilayer nanostructure for its forthcoming characterization.

articleTitle: Ni-Mn-In-V Heusler Alloy New Functional Material for Micro-Bio-Nanomanipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Magnetic field-driven bionanomanipulation continues to be a challenging task because the force applied by current magnetic nanoparticles and nanoactuators is effectively limited to femto and pico Newtons at the proper field and gradient scales. Therefore, of particular interest is search for the new functional materials and new effects that provide a breakthrough opportunity for the influence of a remotely controlled magnetic field on a nano and micro Newton scale on living biological objects, such as bacteria, viruses, individual cells, etc. This work includes deep study of the structure, physical and multifunctional properties of a new family of Heusler Ni-Mn-In-V alloys demonstrating the magnetic shape memory effect responsible for actuation, shape change and the production of mechanical work on objects such as viruses and bacteria in a constant temperature environment. The possibilities of capturing, storing, processing of bionanoobjects are discussed.

articleTitle: Thickness-Dependent Ferroelectric and Piezoelectric Characterization of HfxZr1-xO Nanofilms and Properties Analysis Using FEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As electronic devices continue to advance towards higher integration and smaller sizes, Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin films have become the choice for new nano-device applications due to their high dielectric constant, stable ferroelectric polarization, and high piezoelectric response. We used pulsed laser deposition (PLD) to fabricate HZO thin films of varying thicknesses and discussed the thickness dependence of their piezoelectric and ferroelectric properties using FEM analysis. A multi-physics field coupling finite element simulation model of HZO thin films was constructed based on P-E hysteresis loops and piezoelectric butterfly test curves. The thickness of the HZO film (5-30 nm) affects its polarization behavior. With increasing thickness, the ferroelectricity gradually weakens, the area of the hysteresis loop tends towards zero, which affects its piezoelectric response and ferroelectric stability. Piezo-response force microscopy testing of the piezoelectric butterfly curve shows that at smaller thicknesses, the asymmetry between the positive and negative voltage polarization responses increases, leading to a higher piezoelectric coefficient. This asymmetry is mainly dominated by polarization relaxation effects, which is also reflected in the change of the piezoelectric coefficient under alternating current excitation. The ferroelectric-piezoelectric finite element model developed in this study predicts the characterization of nano-level HZO thin films under different conditions, including thickness, bias voltage, and pre-stress. This helps optimize the design and performance of HZO-based nanodevices.

articleTitle: Modeling of PneuNets Actuators as a Series of Prismatic Pressure Vessels Interacting via Membrane Contact Forces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the popular PneuNets bending actuators consisting of a series of elastomeric chambers bonded to an inextensible layer. The chambers are treated as prismatic pressure vessels where the internal pressure creates volume-defined edge bending moments, applied to the inextensible layer. The resulting free-end bending model displays fluctuating curvature along the actuator axis with maxima beneath the segments bridging two adjacent chambers. Timoshenko-like additional bending angle from shear strains in the inextensible layer is explicitly modeled. When the PneuNets tip is in contact with an external obstacle, the tip force is estimated from the equilibrium of moments of a cut containing the tip chamber. The elastomer behavior is described with ɚ neo-Hookean model. The largest contribution to the free-end bending angle comes from inextensible layer bending rather than from membrane contact forces between neighboring chambers. The opposite is true for the respective contributions to the tip force when the tip is constrained. We developed a neo-Hookean contact model for the membrane contact force acting on the tip chamber, allowing us to predict the tip force for varying inter-chamber gap lengths. The obtained analytical and Finite Element results are compared with experimental data.

articleTitle: Development of a Micromanipulator Robot Based on Four Micropipettes for Multicellular Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper presents a micromanipulator robot system for multicellular manipulation. Four cartesian robot arms with micropipette are responsible for not only traditional cell holding and cell injection but also cell transfer and cell collection. The micropipettes are driven by a self-build syringe-based pneumatic pump module. A close-loop controller based on PID is used for the pump regulating. The precision motion used in the systems are driven by a customized minimum control system based on ARM. A dual field of view optical system with dual image was employed for visual acquiring, where the large visual field is for multicellular supervising and the smaller is for single cell injection. The cells are recognized via the Hough gradient method in both visual fields. Besides, the vision tracking is realized in the smaller visual field via SORT method. To achieve the full-automatic multicellular manipulation, an operation strategy is designed and carried out in the prototype of the proposed robot system. The results show that the robot system is feasible and high performance.

articleTitle: LCI-YOLOv8: A Lightweight Model Based on Modified YOLOv8 for Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Cell target detection plays a crucial role in the fields of bio-immunology, biophysics, and immunology. Existing lightweight cell detection models struggle with low accuracy due to limited laboratory resources and a high proportion of small objects in images, which makes it difficult to balance performance and resource consumption. This paper optimized the existing YOLOv8 architecture as a to achieve lightweight cell images (LCI) detection. Firstly, a Dilation Wise Residual (DWR) two-step expanded residual architecture with partial convolution is raised to increase the receptive field during feature fusion and ignore redundant information, thereby enhancing the model's ability to recognize small objects and reduce model size. Secondly, a sliding window-based local attention method (SLA) is introduced, which improves the model's focus on key information in the detection head with no parameter increasing. At last, the structure of neck part is modified to fuse features better. Experimental results show that compared to the baseline model, the modified YOLOv8 model (LCI-YOLOv8) requires less computational power which achieves a large reduce of 42% of the calculation quantity and 51% reduce of parameters with no precision loss compared to baseline. This approach effectively enhances lightweight performance. However, the LCI-YOLOv8 model still has room for improvement in recall rate when dealing with high-density small objects, which is planned to address in future research.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Forward Transfer – Current Approaches and Perspectives for 4D Printing of Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Direct digital manufacturing is one of the key competencies for accelerating rapid prototyping or the production of individually designed products. Laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) is a frequently used direct digital manufacturing tool for prototyping and production. In this work, the LIFT process was used to print anodes and cathodes which match each other regarding the areal capacity. For this purpose, the transferred voxel density of the anodes was adjusted to match the areal capacity of the cathodes. Subsequently, the electrodes were assembled as a full-cell in pouch cell design. At the end of the electrochemical priming, the cells reach a charge capacity of up to 151 mAh/g, and more than 400 cycles could be achieved at a C-rate of C/2, including the C-rate analysis, before reaching the end-of-life.

articleTitle: Rapid Detection of Four Foodborne Pathogens Based on Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: At present, with the improvement of people's living standards, food borne pathogens, as one of the biggest threats to food safety, are widely valued by people. Therefore, it is urgent to create a fast and efficient method for detecting foodborne pathogens. This article discusses the establishment of a fast and non-destructive detection method for foodborne pathogenic bacteria using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. In this study, the bacterial dry powder of Cronobacter sakazakii was mixed with polyethylene with different mass ratios (0 %, 1 %, 5 %, 10 %, 20 %, 30 %, 40 %, 50 %, 100 % w/w) to make tablet, the thickness of the tablet is 1~1.4 mm, and the diameter is 1.4 cm, and the mass is 0.18 g. Transmission spectrum was used for detection. By observed and analyzed the absorption spectra, the waveforms of three groups of repeated data showed consistency, and there were obvious characteristic absorption peaks at 1.28 and 1.78 THz. The accuracy of clustering software analysis results is 100 %, which shows that the method has good stability and specificity. The detection limit of Cronobacter sakazakii is 1%. We have successfully established a terahertz time-domain spectral detection method for foodborne pathogens. This method is rapid, stable and sensitive, and has a broad application prospect.

articleTitle: The Role of Exercise Intervention on Insulin Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) refers to the decrease of insulin sensitivity and the insensitivity of the body to insulin. The normal concentration of insulin cannot maintain the normal level of blood sugar, and no matter how much insulin is secreted, it cannot achieve good hypoglycemic effect, thus causing diabetes. The major target organs and tissues of IR are liver, fat and skeletal muscle. IR can be improved by lifestyle intervention, such as diet and exercise control. Exercise is a non-drug intervention to prevent and treat IR. The clinical application of exercise is more and more extensive. Because it is more convenient, economical and effective. In this article, the pathogenesis and pathophysiological process of insulin resistance are reviewed. The mechanism of intervention of exercise on insulin resistance is combed, so as to try to find the best exercise prescription for improving IR and provide useful reference for clinics.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Surface Roughness Analysis for Polymer-Based Products: Integrating Laser Speckle Contrast and Stylus Profilometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study introduces a novel approach for measuring surface roughness in polymer-based samples using laser speckle photometry principles, offering potential for non-contact and non-destructive in-process measurements. A methodology for characterising surface roughness offline for polymer samples is outlined, utilising stylus profilometry, a technique not commonly employed in polymer manufacturing. Investigations into the reliability and stability of laser speckle on polymer-based products with various shape profiles were conducted, resulting in successful outcomes through mean intensity matching techniques. This enabled the correlation of surface roughness with two laser speckle statistical parameters: laser speckle contrast and binary digitization techniques. This research provides valuable insights for advancing surface roughness measurement techniques in polymer manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Chemoattractant-Dependent Neutrophil Migration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Here we developed an in vitro model system for study a dynamic process of neutrophil granulocytes migration under the influence of two main chemoattractants responsible for neutrophil transendothelial migration: leukotriene B4 (direct migration) and lipoxin A4 (reverse migration). For the first time migration in such model was studied using scanning probe microscopy method: scanning ion-conductance microscopy, which allowed to observe neutrophil’s membrane-cytoskeleton complex stiffness modulations. Thus, Young’s modulus of the neutrophil membrane-cytoskeleton complex increased during movement, while after firm adhesion to substrate it decreased. At the same time, mobility of cells adhered to solid substrate (Petri dish surface) was reduced. These neutrophil granulocytes were also more sensitive to probe impact and cell death was visualized during scanning in the system with chemoattractant. Rigidity of the cell during necrosis dying was also decreasing. Usage of the endothelial monolayer as the substrate prevented so firm adhesion of neutrophils, however their binding to the endothelial cells were strong enough to perform continuous scanning during 30 minutes. Migration in the model with endothelial monolayer was more pronounced and allowed most neutrophils to move, while polymer substrate provoked cells adhesion.

articleTitle: Bioinspired Surfaces for Directional Liquid Transport: Design and Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Controllable directional liquid transport, as a promising form of intelligent liquid manipulation, plays an important role in many fields. In nature, directional liquid transport properties are found on a wide variety of biological surfaces, such as the Namib Desert beetle, cactus and Crassula muscosa, etc. Learning from nature provides great inspiration for researchers to solve engineering problems. In this review, the classical directional transport mechanisms, including the wettability gradient and the Laplace pressure difference, are introduced. Then, from single to multiple biomimetic surfaces, the design and manufacturing are reviewed in detail through some representative examples. Finally, some challenges faced in the current development of bioinspired surfaces are summarized.
